readSections: Introduction; §§1.1–1.4; §§2.1–2.3; §§3.1–3.3; §§4.1–4.7; references and final page: all98 published PDF pages

summary: Full main-paper extraction of tame parahoric integral Shimura models, with minuscule fixer embeddings, punctured-Witt-disc torsor purity, corrected tensor displays, abelian-type descent and nearby-cycle test functions. Partial because recursive original-source and declaration-sized proof closure remains explicit; no implementation claim. Reviewed by REV-PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18 (Claude Code, cc-2aeb03) and corrected in place: 275 items (14 library, 14 planned, 247 missing), 80 mistakes recorded (57 misprints, 14 gaps, 9 errors). Not formalised.

theorem reductiveCommHopfAlgProperty_iff (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (H : FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.{u, u} k) :
    reductiveCommHopfAlgProperty k H ↔
      Algebra.Smooth k H ∧
        geometricallyConnectedCommHopfAlgProperty k H.obj ∧
          ∀ I : HopfIdeal (AlgebraicClosure k)
              (FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.baseChange (K := AlgebraicClosure k) H),
            I.IsNormal →
              geometricallyConnectedCommHopfAlgProperty (AlgebraicClosure k)
                (FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.quotient
                  (FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.baseChange (K := AlgebraicClosure k) H) I).obj →
              smoothUnipotentCommHopfAlgProperty (AlgebraicClosure k)

structure AbelianVariety (K : Type u) [Field K] where
  /-- The underlying group scheme over `Spec K`. -/
  toOver : Over (Spec (.of K))

  grpObj : GrpObj toOver

declarations.statementRead:
structure DividedPowers where
  /-- The divided power function underlying a divided power structure -/
  dpow : ℕ → A → A
  dpow_null : ∀ {n x} (_ : x ∉ I), dpow n x = 0
  dpow_zero : ∀ {x} (_ : x ∈ I), dpow 0 x = 1
  dpow_one : ∀ {x} (_ : x ∈ I), dpow 1 x = x
  dpow_mem : ∀ {n x} (_ : n ≠ 0) (_ : x ∈ I), dpow n x ∈ I
  dpow_add : ∀ {n} {x y} (_ : x ∈ I) (_ : y ∈ I),
    dpow n (x + y) = (antidiagonal n).sum fun k ↦ dpow k.1 x * dpow k.2 y
  dpow_mul : ∀ {n} {a : A} {x} (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow n (a * x) = a ^ n * dpow n x
  mul_dpow : ∀ {m n} {x} (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow m x * dpow n x = choose (m + n) m * dpow (m + n) x
  dpow_comp : ∀ {m n x} (_ : n ≠ 0) (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow m (dpow n x) = uniformBell m n * dpow (m * n) x

variable (A) in
/-- The canonical `DividedPowers` structure on the zero ideal -/

qualifications: Every cited declaration was statement-read at the pinned commits in this session; reused carriers retain their exact scope.
Witt vectors do not supply the Zink subring, frames, displays or integral comparison.
The characteristic-zero TauCeti.IsMinuscule and Q-algebra YoungTableau.weylModule are near misses for the characteristic-p group representations.
The Kostant coordinate-root tangent theorem supplies a concrete matrix differential; its abstract pinned group/Grassmannian adapter is still required.

items.name: Witt-vector coefficient carrier
items.statement: For prime p and perfect field k of characteristic p use the existing p-typical Witt vectors W(k), with coefficient sequence indexed by natural numbers; its fraction field supplies L. This item is only the coefficient carrier, not a crystalline site.

uses.where: KP18 §§1–4, foundational carrier imported with the limited scope below
uses.how: For p>2 and a complete Noetherian local R with perfect residue k, W_hat(R) is the Zink subring W(k)⊕W_hat(m_R), where the second summand consists of Witt coordinates tending m_R-adically to zero; I_R is the kernel of W_hat(R)→R.

uses.where: KP18 §§1–4, foundational carrier imported with the limited scope below
uses.how: A frame is (S,I,φ,φ1) with I+pS⊂Jac(S), φ a Frobenius lift modulo p, φ1:I→S φ-semilinear with generating image, and φ|_I=pφ1; strict maps preserve these maps and ideals.

items.name: Kottwitz component homomorphism
items.statement: (§1.1.2, printed pp. 127–128; black box from Haines–Rapoport [38, Prop. 3 and Remarks 4, 11].) Let G be a connected reductive group over K, I the inertia group, κ_G: G(K^ur) → π_1(G)_I the Kottwitz homomorphism, G(K^ur)_1 := ker κ_G. Let Ω ⊂ B(G,K) be a non-empty bounded subset contained in an apartment, Ω̄ its image in B(G^ad,K), G(K^ur)_Ω ⊂ G(K^ur)_Ω̄ the pointwise fixers, and G(K^ur)_Ω° = 𝒢_Ω°(O^ur) the connected stabilizer. Then G(K^ur)_Ω° = G(K^ur)_Ω̄ ∩ G(K^ur)_1 = G(K^ur)_Ω ∩ G(K^ur)_1. Hence G(K)_Ω° = G(K)_Ω ∩ ker κ_G, and by [11, (1.7.6)] the parahoric group scheme 𝒢_x° depends only on G and the image x̄ of x in B(G^ad,K). If G is semisimple and simply connected, κ_G is trivial and G(K)_Ω° = G(K)_Ω.

items.name: Exact central quotient of connected parahorics
items.statement: (Prop. 1.1.4, (1.1.5), printed p. 128; Remark 1.1.8, printed p. 129.) In the setting of 1.1.3 (α: G → G̃ a central extension with kernel Z, x ∈ B(G,K), x̃ = α_*(x)), suppose G splits over a tamely ramified extension of K and Z is either a torus or finite of rank prime to p. Let 𝒵 be the (smooth) schematic closure of Z in 𝒢_x°. Then 1 → 𝒵 → 𝒢_x° →^α 𝒢̃_x̃° → 1 is an fppf exact sequence of group schemes over Spec(O). Remark 1.1.8 (justified only by 'similar arguments'): under the same assumptions, the schematic closure of Z in 𝒢_x is smooth over O and equals ker(α: 𝒢_x → 𝒢̃_x̃). In general α: 𝒢_x → 𝒢̃_x̃ is not fppf surjective, for example when 𝒢_x = 𝒢_x° but 𝒢̃_x̃ ≠ 𝒢̃_x̃°.

items.name: Periodic graded lattice chain
items.statement: (§1.1.9, printed p. 130.) Let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space. A periodic lattice chain is a non-empty set {Λ} of O-lattices in V that is totally ordered by inclusion and stable under multiplication by scalars (K^×). A grading is a function c: {Λ} → R that is strictly decreasing for inclusion and satisfies c(π^nΛ) = c(Λ) + n. By [12, Prop. 1.8, Th. 2.11], the points of B(GL(V),K) are in 1-1 correspondence with graded periodic lattice chains ({Λ},c). For such a chain there are an integer r ≥ 1 (the period) and distinct lattices Λ^0,…,Λ^{r−1} with πΛ^0 ⊂ Λ^{r−1} ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ Λ^1 ⊂ Λ^0 (1.1.10) and {Λ} = {Λ^i}_{i∈Z}, where Λ^{mr+i} := π^mΛ^i for m ∈ Z and 0 ≤ i < r. The stabilizer GL(V)_x of the corresponding point x is ⋂_{i=0}^{r−1} GL(Λ^i) ⊂ GL(V).

items.name: Almost self-dual symplectic chain
items.statement: (§1.1.11, printed pp. 130–131.) Let ψ: V × V → K be a perfect alternating K-bilinear form and set Λ^∨ := {v ∈ V | ψ(v,x) ∈ O for all x ∈ Λ}. The points of B(GSp(V),K) are in 1-1 correspondence with 'almost self-dual' graded periodic lattice chains ({Λ},c): {Λ} is stable under Λ ↦ Λ^∨, and c(Λ^∨) = −c(Λ) + m for some m ∈ Z independent of Λ. Hence B(GSp(V),K) ⊂ B(GL(V),K) (a variant of [13]). For such a chain there are r ≥ 1, distinct lattices Λ^0,…,Λ^{r−1} and a ∈ {0,1} such that Λ^{r−1} ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ Λ^0 ⊂ (Λ^0)^∨ ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ (Λ^{r−1})^∨ ⊂ π^{−1}Λ^{r−1} (1.1.12) and (Λ^i)^∨ = Λ^{−i−a} for each i. The chain consists of all scalar multiples of the Λ^i and (Λ^i)^∨. The stabilizer of the corresponding x is GSp(V)_x = GSp(V) ∩ GL(V)_x.

items.name: Diagonal chain stabilizer is a closed immersion
items.statement: (§1.1.9, printed p. 130; §1.1.11, printed p. 131.) (i) GL case [12, 3.8, 3.9]: for x ↔ ({Λ^i},c), the parahoric group scheme 𝒢ℒ_x is the schematic (Zariski) closure of the diagonal GL(V) ↪ ∏_{i=0}^{r−1} GL(V) in ∏_{i=0}^{r−1} GL(Λ^i). It is identified with the group scheme Aut(Λ^•) of automorphisms of the indexed chain Λ^• = {Λ^i}_{i∈Z}, because the latter is smooth ([64, Appendix to Ch. 3]) and has the same O^ur-points. (ii) GSp case: 𝒢𝒮𝒫_x is the schematic closure of the diagonal GSp(V) ↪ ∏_{i=−(r−1)−a}^{r−1} GL(V) in ∏_{i=−(r−1)−a}^{r−1} GL(Λ^i). By [64, Appendix to Ch. 3] it equals the group scheme Aut({Λ^i}_{i∈Z}, ψ_i) of automorphisms of the chain that respect the perfect pairings ψ_i: Λ^i × Λ^{−i−a} → O induced by ψ up to a common similitude. (iii) For a finite-dimensional central division K-algebra D and a right D-module V, the paper says only that [12] gives 'a similar description' of B(GL(V)_D,K) and its parahoric subgroups, and it names the parahoric group scheme (𝒢ℒ(V)_D)_x.

items.name: Based toral building map
items.statement: (Prop. 1.2.3, printed p. 132; setting of 1.2.2.) Let G be split over K, G_O a reductive model over O, and x_o a hyperspecial vertex of B(G,K) with stabilizer G_O(O), also viewed in B(G,K^ur). Let ρ: G → GL(V) be a K-representation (not necessarily faithful) with V = ⊕_i V_i, where each ρ_i: G → GL(V_i) is irreducible (hence absolutely irreducible) and factors as G →^{a_i} G_i ↪ GL(V_i) with a_i an epimorphism onto the split reductive G_i. If K = k((π)), assume each a_i induces a separable morphism from each root subgroup of G onto its image in G_i. Let Λ_i ⊂ V_i be O-lattices with ρ_i(G_O(O^ur)) ⊂ GL(Λ_i ⊗_O O^ur), and set Λ := (⊕_iΛ_i) ⊗_O O^ur. Then there is a Gal(K^ur/K)- and G(K^ur)-equivariant toral map ι: B(G,K^ur) → B(GL(V),K^ur) (1.2.4) such that ι(x_o) = [Λ] = ({π^nΛ}_{n∈Z}, c_Λ), where c_Λ(π^nΛ) = n. If in addition ρ is faithful, ι is an isometric embedding and is the unique Gal(K^ur/K)- and G(K^ur)-equivariant toral embedding with this ι(x_o). By restriction it gives a G(K)-equivariant toral isometric embedding ι: B(G,K) → B(GL(V),K).

items.name: Quotient group preserves the chosen lattice
items.statement: (Lemma 1.2.5, printed p. 132, inside the proof of Prop. 1.2.3.) Keep the notation of Prop. 1.2.3. Let x_{o,i} ∈ B(G_i,K) be the (hyperspecial) image of x_o under the canonical toral map a_i: B(G,K^ur) → B(G_i,K^ur) of [48, Thm. 2.1.8], and let G_{i,O} be the corresponding reductive O-model, so that a_i extends to a_{i,O}: G_O → G_{i,O}. Then G_{i,O}(O^ur) ⊂ GL(Λ_i ⊗_O O^ur), and G_i ↪ GL(V_i) extends to an O-group scheme homomorphism G_{i,O} → GL(Λ_i). (The proof notes that a_{i,O}(O^ur) need not be surjective. It uses that a_i maps root subgroups isomorphically onto root subgroups, integrally so, together with the X^•(𝒯_i)-grading of Λ_i, and the fact that G_{i,O}(O^ur) is generated by the 𝒰_i(O^ur) and 𝒯_i(O^ur) [11, 4.6].)

items.name: Minuscule representation in characteristic zero
items.statement: (§1.2.9, printed p. 134.) Assume char(K) = 0 (for the rest of §1.2 unless K = k((π)) is explicitly discussed). Let T ⊂ G be a maximal torus. A representation ρ: G → GL(V) is minuscule if ρ ⊗_K K̄ is isomorphic to a direct sum of irreducible representations each of which is minuscule in this sense: the weights of the corresponding representation of Lie(G^der_K̄) for the Cartan subalgebra Lie(T^der_K̄) are all conjugate under the Weyl group ([7, Ch. VI, §1, ex. 24; §4, ex. 15]). The notion does not depend on T. For G = SL_2 the irreducible minuscule representations are the standard and the trivial one; in particular trivial summands are allowed.

items.name: Integral highest-weight lattice with pinning
items.statement: (§1.2.12, printed p. 135.) Let G be split over K and ρ: G → GL(V) a K-representation. Let H be the split Chevalley form of G over Z_p with a pinning (T_H, B_H, e), and x_o the hyperspecial vertex of B(H,Q_p) with stabilizer H(Z_p). This x_o is also viewed as a hyperspecial vertex of B(G,K') for every p-adic field K' ⊃ K, via B(H,Q_p) ↪ B(H,K'). Fix G ≃ H ⊗_{Z_p} K and take G_O = H ⊗_{Z_p} O. Write V = ⊕_iV_i, ρ = ⊕_iρ_i, with V_i = V(λ_i) ⊗_{Q_p} K and V(λ_i) the irreducible Weyl module over Q_p of highest weight λ_i. Fix a highest weight vector v_i and set Λ_i := 𝔘_H^− · v_i ⊂ V(λ_i), where 𝔘_H^− is the Z_p-subalgebra of the (Kostant/distribution) enveloping algebra 𝔘_H of H generated by the negative root spaces. This gives ρ_i: H → GL(Λ_i) (cf. [41]), and the lattices Λ_i ⊗_{Z_p} O satisfy the hypotheses of Prop. 1.2.3. Hence there is ι: B(G,K^ur) → B(GL(V),K^ur) (1.2.13) with ι(x_o) the point of Λ ⊗_{Z_p} O^ur = (⊕_iΛ_i) ⊗ O^ur. More generally ι may depend on reals t_i as in Remark 1.2.7(c); the choice above is t_i = 0. If ρ is faithful, ι is an embedding.

items.name: Tame projective descent of an irreducible representation
items.statement: (§1.2.15 with (1.2.16)–(1.2.20), printed pp. 136–137; follows [69], [66].) Keep the setting of 1.2.14: G splits over a tame K̃/K with Γ = Gal(K̃/K), ψ: G_K̃ ≅ H_K̃, cocycle c. Let ρ: G → GL(V) be K-irreducible (not necessarily faithful). D^0 := {φ ∈ End_K(V) | φρ(g) = ρ(g)φ for all g ∈ G(K̃)} is a division K-algebra, and V is a right module over D := (D^0)^opp. Γ acts on dominant weights ([69, 3.1]). V_{λ,K̃} ⊂ V ⊗_K K̃ is the span of the simple submodules of highest weight λ. Let λ_1,…,λ_r be the λ with V_{λ,K̃} ≠ 0; this set is Γ-stable, V ⊗_K K̃ = ⊕_i V_{λ_i,K̃}, Γ permutes the summands transitively (compatibly with its action on {λ_i}), and V_{λ_i,K̃} ≃ V(λ_i)^{⊕d} ⊗_{Q_p} K̃ with d independent of i. Let Γ_1 = Stab_Γ(λ_1), K_1 = K̃^{Γ_1}, V_1 = V_{λ_1,K̃}. Then Z(D) = K_1, V ⊗_{K_1} K̃ ≃ V_1, and there is an absolutely irreducible K_1-representation ρ̄_1: G_{K_1} → GL(V)_D with ρ̄_1 ⊗_{K_1} K̃ = ρ_1: G_K̃ ≅ H_K̃ → GL(V(λ_1)_K̃). Also ρ = Res_{K_1/K}(Res_{D/K_1} ∘ ρ̄_1) (1.2.17), i.e. ρ is the composite (1.2.18)–(1.2.19). Explicitly: J_1(K̃) ⊂ Aut(H)(K̃) is generated by H^ad(K̃) and the c(γ), γ ∈ Γ_1. Schur's lemma gives a homomorphism θ: J_1(K̃) → PGL(V(λ_1) ⊗ K̃) with ρ_1 ∘ a = θ(a) ∘ ρ_1 (1.2.20). The cocycle c' := θ∘c: Γ_1 → PGL(V(λ_1) ⊗ K̃) defines End(V)_D = End(V(λ_1) ⊗ K̃)^{Γ_1}, and ρ_1 descends to ρ̄_1: G_{K_1} = (H ⊗ K̃)^{Γ_1} → GL(V)_D = GL(V(λ_1) ⊗ K̃)^{Γ_1}, the fixed points taken for the c- and c'-twisted actions ([69, Thm. 3.3]).
items.locator: §1.2.15, displays (1.2.16)–(1.2.20), printed pp. 136–137 (setting from §1.2.14, printed pp. 135–136)

items.name: Galois-equivariant minuscule building map
items.statement: (Prop. 1.2.21, printed pp. 137–138; 1.2.22–1.2.26, printed p. 138.) Assume K̃ ⊃ K^ur, and assume ρ (equivalently ρ_1) is minuscule. Equip B(GL(V(λ_1)),K̃) with the Γ_1-action induced by the standard action on GL(V(λ_1) ⊗ K̃) twisted by c'. Then the G(K̃) = H(K̃)-equivariant toral map ι_1: B(G,K̃) = B(H,K̃) → B(GL(V(λ_1)),K̃) of the split case (1.2.13) is Γ_1-equivariant. (Proof: reduce to ρ_1 faithful and compare with Landvogt's Γ_1-equivariant ι_1^L via Cor. 1.2.11.) Consequently (1.2.22), taking I_1-fixed points ([60]) gives ι_1: B(G,K_1^ur) → B(GL(V)_D,K_1^ur) (1.2.23), and similarly for t + ι_1. Composing B(G,K^ur) ⊂ B(G,K_1^ur) → B(GL(V)_D,K_1^ur) with the map induced by forgetting the O_D-structure of lattices gives a G(K^ur)- and Gal(K^ur/K)-equivariant toral map ι: B(G,K^ur) → B(GL(V),K^ur) (1.2.24). For general minuscule ρ = ⊕_jρ_j, combining the ι_j with the Levi embedding (1.2.25) gives a G(K^ur)- and Gal(K^ur/K)-equivariant toral map, which is injective if ρ is faithful (1.2.26). [See sourceIssues: the 1.2.24 step as written needs K_1/K totally ramified; in general it must be replaced by the product over the K-embeddings of K_1.]
proofSteps: Compare with a Galois-equivariant Landvogt map by a real central translation; Galois acts trivially on that translation direction.

items.name: Equal-characteristic twisted minuscule representation data
items.statement: (§1.2.27, printed p. 139.) Let K = k((π)) and G a reductive group over K split over a tamely ramified K̃/K, with a representation ρ: G → GL(V). Assume, as part of the data, that ρ is a direct sum of G-representations each obtained by restriction of scalars as in (1.2.17) from a representation ρ̄_1 that is a twisted Weyl module for a minuscule dominant weight λ, the twist being given exactly as in the char-0 construction of 1.2.15. (Such decompositions are not automatic, since G-representations need not be semisimple.) A dominant weight λ of a Chevalley group is minuscule if there is no dominant μ with μ < λ; then the Weyl module V(λ)_k is simple and its weights are W·λ ([41, II 2.15]). Under these assumptions the maps ι_1 of Prop. 1.2.21 and ι of (1.2.26) are obtained by the same construction; H → H/ker(ρ_1) is separable on each root subgroup (cf. the SL_2 reduction in the proof of Prop. 1.3.3), so Prop. 1.2.3 applies.

items.name: Rank-one minuscule root strings
items.statement: Let G be split over K with maximal split torus T, and ρ: G → GL(V) faithful and minuscule (first with G semisimple and ρ irreducible, so all weight spaces V_λ, λ ∈ W(ρ) = W·λ0, are lines). For a root a ∈ Φ(G,T) let G_a = ⟨U_a, U_{-a}⟩ (≅ SL_2 or PSL_2) and ρ_a: SL_2 → G_a → GL(V). As a Lie(G_a) ≅ sl_2-module, V = ⊕_[λ] V_[λ] with V_[λ] = ⊕_{λ' ∈ [λ]} V_{λ'}, where [λ] is the class of λ ∈ W(ρ) modulo Z·a; each class is either {λ} (V_[λ] trivial) or {λ, λ+a} (V_[λ] the standard representation). Hence ρ_a is minuscule, does not factor through PSL_2, and G_a ≅ SL_2.

items.name: Pappas–Zhu polynomial group and global Grassmannian
items.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite unramified, G/K connected reductive splitting over a tame extension, and x ∈ B(G,K). [59, §§3–4, Thm. 4.1] give a smooth affine group scheme 𝒢̲ over O[u] with 𝒢̲ ⊗_{O[u],u↦p} O = 𝒢 := 𝒢°_x and with G̲ = 𝒢̲|_{O[u,u^{-1}]} reductive. [59, §6] gives the ind-projective global affine Grassmannian Gr_{𝒢̲,A^1} → A^1 = Spec O[u]. Its R-points over x ∈ A^1(R) are the 𝒢̲-torsors on A^1_R with a trivialization off the graph of x. Its base change along O[u] → K, u ↦ p, is identified (via t = u − p) with the affine Grassmannian Gr_{G,K}, the fpqc sheafification of R ↦ G(R((t)))/G(R[[t]]).

items.name: Central quotient map of polynomial models

items.name: Polynomial extension of the lattice-chain representation
items.statement: (Proof of Prop. 2.3.7, Steps 1–3, printed pp. 158–162.) Let L = Q_p^ur, O = O_L with residue field k, and 𝒢̲ the Pappas–Zhu group scheme over O[u] attached to (G_L, x) (§2.1.4). Write ρ = ⊕_j ρ_j with ρ_j irreducible over Q_p, and let ρ'_{j,L}: G_L → GL(V'_{j,L}) be the restriction of scalars from L_j = L·Q_{p,j1} to L of the descended Weyl module ρ'_{j,L_j}: G_{L_j} → GL(V'_j), V'_j = (V(λ_{j1})⊗Q̃_p)^{I_{j1}}. Step 1: ρ'_{j,L} extends to ρ̲'_{j,O[u^{±1}]}: G̲ → GL_{d_j}(O[u^{±1}]), d_j = e_j·dim_{L_j}V'_j (via (2.3.11)–(2.3.14)), in a basis for which ρ'_{j,L}(S) lies in the diagonal torus. Step 2: this extends to ρ̲'_{j,O[u]}: 𝒢̲ → Aut_{O[u]}(N_{j,•}) for the periodic O[u]-lattice chain N_{j,•} = Λ'_• ∩ O[u^{±1}]^{d_j} determined by y_{j,L} = ι_{j,L}(x), and ρ̲_{O[u]} = ∏_j∏_τ ρ̲'_{j,O[u]}: 𝒢̲ → ℋ = ∏_j∏_τ Aut_{O[u]}(N_{j,•}) extends ρ_L. Step 3: ρ̲_{O[u]} ⊗ k((u)) is minuscule of the kind in 1.2.27 and ρ̲_{O[u]} satisfies condition (*) of [59, 8.1.1] (by 1.3.13).
proofSteps: Normalize the highest-vector Galois lifts, use tame fixed modules and polynomial bundle freeness, extend by the intersection of coordinate rings, then apply the equal-characteristic fixer theorem.

items.name: Polarized total lattice
items.statement: (§2.3.15) Let 𝒢𝒮𝒫_z be the stabilizer of the periodic (almost) self-dual lattice chain ℒ = {Λ^i}_{i∈Z} in V, indexed as in 1.1.11 so that (Λ^i)^∨ = Λ^{−i−a}, a ∈ {0,1}. items.name: Dieudonné display
items.statement: (§3.1.3, following [73]) A Dieudonné display over R is a tuple (M,M_1,Φ,Φ_1): (i) M a finite free Ŵ(R)-module; (ii) M_1 ⊂ M a Ŵ(R)-submodule with I_R M ⊂ M_1 ⊂ M and M/M_1 a projective R-module; (iii) Φ: M → M φ-semilinear; (iv) Φ_1: M_1 → M φ-semilinear, with image generating M, and Φ_1(V(w)m) = wΦ(m) for w ∈ Ŵ(R), m ∈ M. Then Φ(m) = pΦ_1(m) for m ∈ M_1. When W(R) is p-torsion free (e.g. R p-torsion free, or pR = 0 and R reduced), Φ is determined by Φ(m) = Φ_1(V(1)m), and a triple (M,M_1,Φ_1) satisfying (i), (ii) and the first part of (iv) is also called a Dieudonné display.

items.name: Normal decomposition and linearized display map
items.statement: (Lemma 3.1.5) Suppose W(R) is p-torsion free. Let M be a free Ŵ(R)-module, M_1 ⊂ M a submodule with I_R M ⊂ M_1 and M/M_1 a projective R-module, and M = L ⊕ T a normal decomposition. (a) M̃_1 ≅ φ*(L) ⊕ pφ*(T) ≅ Ŵ(R)^d with d = rk M; in particular M̃_1 depends only on the reduction of (M,M_1) modulo p. (b) If (M,M_1,Φ_1) is a Dieudonné display over R, the linearization Φ_1^#: φ*M_1 → M factors as φ*M_1 → M̃_1 →^Ψ M with Ψ a Ŵ(R)-module isomorphism. (c) Conversely, given an isomorphism Ψ: M̃_1 = Im(φ*M_1 → φ*M) ≅ M, there is a unique Dieudonné display (M,M_1,Φ_1) over R which produces (M,M_1,Ψ) by (b).

items.name: Dieudonné antiequivalence with displays
items.statement: (§3.1.7) Let 𝒢 be a p-divisible group over R (R as in §3.1.2, p > 2) with contravariant Dieudonné crystal D(𝒢). By the main theorem of [73], D(𝒢)(Ŵ(R)) has a natural structure of Dieudonné display over R, and 𝒢 ↦ D(𝒢)(Ŵ(R)) is an anti-equivalence between p-divisible groups over R and Dieudonné displays over R ([73] uses the covariant crystal; the paper composes with Cartier duality). Under this anti-equivalence, base change of Dieudonné displays (§3.1.6) corresponds to base change of p-divisible groups ([50, Thm. 3.19]).

items.statement: (§3.1.8) Let 𝒢_0 be a p-divisible group over k, D = D(𝒢_0)(W) with Dieudonné display (D,D_1,Φ,Φ_1), given (Lemma 3.1.5) by Ψ_0: D̃_1 = φ*(D_1) ≅ D. Put M = D ⊗_W Ŵ(R), let M̄_1 ⊂ M/I_R M = D ⊗_W R be the direct summand corresponding to gPg^{−1} for the universal point g ∈ (GL(D)/P)(R), M_1 ⊂ M its preimage, and Ψ: M̃_1 ≅ M any Ŵ(R)-linear isomorphism reducing to Ψ_0 modulo m_R. Then (M,M_1,Ψ) is a Dieudonné display over R and so corresponds to a p-divisible group 𝒢_R over R deforming 𝒢_0.

items.statement: (§3.2.5) Let P ⊂ GL(D) be the fixed lift of the parabolic P_0 ⊂ GL(D⊗_W k) of the filtration on D⊗_W k, M^loc = GL(D)/P, and Spf R = M̂^loc its completion along the identity. Let K'/K_0 be finite and y: R → K' a K'-point with s_{α,0} ∈ Fil^0 y*(M̄^⊗). Then the stabilizer of y*(M̄_1) ⊂ y*(M̄) is a parabolic P_y ⊂ GL(D) over K', conjugate to P and induced by a G-valued cocharacter μ_y (cited from [43, Lemma 1.4.5], proof corrected in footnote 4). Let E ⊂ K' (E ⊃ K_0) be the local reflex field of μ_y (field of definition of its G-conjugacy class); the orbit G·y ⊂ (GL(D)/P)_{K'} is defined over E, M^loc_G is its closure in (GL(D)/P)_{O_E}, and s_{α,0} ∈ Fil^0 M̄^⊗ over M^loc_G. M̂^loc_G = Spf R_G is the completion of M^loc_G along (the image of) the identity of GL(D⊗_W k); it depends only on the G-conjugacy class of μ_y and on the specialization of y, and R_G is a quotient of R_E = R⊗_W O_E. If G is defined over Q_p, the local model of §2 for μ = μ_y^{-1} (Proposition 2.3.7), base-changed to O_E, is this M^loc_G.

items.name: Breuil–Kisin filtration lattice at a DVR point
items.statement: (§3.2.5, last paragraph; Lemma 3.2.6, first claim) Let K/K_0 be a finite, totally ramified extension with uniformizer π and Eisenstein polynomial E(u) ∈ W[u]. View O_K as an 𝔖 = W[[u]]-algebra via u ↦ π, and set M_𝔖 = D⊗_W 𝔖 (an exception to the convention that M_A is a Ŵ(A)-module). items.name: Integral tensors in the tilde lattice
items.statement: (Lemma 3.2.9) Let ξ: R_G → O_K. Then (1) s_{α,0} ∈ M̃^⊗_{O_K,1} = (M̃_1⊗_{Ŵ(R)} Ŵ(O_K))^⊗, where M̃_{O_K,1} ⊂ φ*(ξ*(M)) = φ*(M_{O_K}) by 3.1.6; (2) T_ξ = Isom_{(s_{α,0})}(M̃_1⊗_{Ŵ(R)}Ŵ(O_K), M⊗_{Ŵ(R)}Ŵ(O_K)) is a 𝒢-torsor over Ŵ(O_K) (the proof shows it is trivial). Proof: use the Frobenius-equivariant map 𝔖 → Ŵ(O_K), u ↦ [π], and a decomposition M_𝔖 = L⊕T with F = L⊕E(u)T. items.name: Tensor-preserving versal display with very-good input
items.statement: (§3.2.12, with the KPZ26 correction) Assume R_G is normal, so Corollary 3.2.11 applies. Assume also (KPZ26 Def. 5.2.5) that the tensors are horizontal ('very good') at the point, which the printed text omits. Let a_{R_E} = m²_{R_E} + π_E R_E, so that R_E/a_{R_E} = R/a_R. Then there is Ψ_{R_G}: M̃_{R_G,1} ≅ M_{R_G} that respects the s_{α,0} and is constant modulo a_{R_E}: its reduction is induced by Ψ_0⊗1 through the (corrected) canonical isomorphism of Lemma 3.1.9. Lift Ψ_{R_G} to any Ψ: M̃_{R_E,1} ≅ M_{R_E} constant mod a_{R_E}. Then (M_{R_E}, M̃_{R_E,1}, Ψ) is a Dieudonné display over R_E. Its p-divisible group 𝒢_{R_E} is versal: if R'_E is a versal deformation O_E-algebra for 𝒢_0, the classifying map j: R'_E → R_E is an isomorphism mod m²+π_E by Lemma 3.1.12, hence an isomorphism, since both rings are smooth over O_E of the same dimension.

items.name: Hodge normalization model
items.statement: Assume a Hodge embedding ι: (G,X) ↪ (GSp(V,ψ),S±) and (4.1.4): G_{Q_p} splits over a tamely ramified extension of Q_p and p ∤ |π_1(G^der)| (p > 2 is the standing assumption of §3, used in §4). Fix x ∈ B(G,Q_p) and let 𝒢 = 𝒢_x be the smooth Z_p-group scheme with generic fibre G that is the stabilizer of x (so 𝒢° is parahoric). After replacing ι by another symplectic embedding (2.3.15, Corollary 2.3.16), 𝒢𝒮𝒫 (the group scheme of ι(x)) is the group scheme of a single Z_p-lattice V_{Z_p} ⊂ V_{Q_p} with V_{Z_p} ⊂ V_{Z_p}^∨, ι induces a closed immersion 𝒢 ↪ 𝒢𝒮𝒫 (Lemma 1.3.3) and an embedding of local models M^loc_{G,X} ↪ M^loc_{GSp,S±}. Fix a Z-lattice V_Z ⊂ V_Q with V_Z ⊗ Z_(p) = V_{Z_p} ∩ V_Q =: V_{Z_(p)} and V_Z ⊂ V_Z^∨; G_{Z_(p)} is the Zariski closure of G in GL(V_{Z_(p)}), so G_{Z_(p)} ⊗ Z_p ≅ 𝒢. Put K_p = 𝒢(Z_p), K'_p = 𝒢𝒮𝒫(Z_p), K = K_pK^p with K^p sufficiently small, and choose K'^p ⊂ GSp(A_f^p) with Sh_K(G,X) ↪ Sh_{K'}(GSp,S±) over E ([43] Lemma 2.1.2). V_Z gives a moduli interpretation of Sh_{K'}(GSp,S±) and an integral model 𝒮_{K'}(GSp,S±) over Z_(p). For a prime v | p of E, 𝒮^−_K(G,X) is the closure of Sh_K(G,X) in 𝒮_{K'}(GSp,S±)_{O_(v)}, and 𝒮_K(G,X) is the normalization of 𝒮^−_K(G,X).

items.name: Absolute Hodge tensors and their realizations
items.statement: Fix tensors (s_α) ⊂ V^⊗_{Z_(p)} whose stabilizer is G_{Z_(p)} ([43] Lemma 1.3.2). Let h: 𝒜 → Sh_K(G,X) be the restriction of the universal abelian scheme and 𝒱 = R^1h_*Ω^•. The s_α give absolute Hodge cycles s_{α,dR} ∈ 𝒱^⊗ defined over E ([43] §2.2). For a field κ ⊃ E of characteristic 0 and x ∈ Sh_K(G,X)(κ), fix embeddings Q_p ↪ C and σ: κ̄ ↪ C. Let s_{α,ét,x} ∈ H^1_ét(𝒜_{x,κ̄},Q_p)^⊗ be the image of s_{α,dR,x} under H^1_dR(𝒜_x) ⊗_{κ,σ} C ≅ H^1_B(𝒜_x(C),Q) ⊗ C ≅ H^1_ét(𝒜_{x,κ̄},Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} C. Then s_{α,ét,x} is Gal(κ̄/κ)-invariant and independent of the choices ([43] Lemma 2.2.1). For x ∈ Sh_K(G,X)(K), K/E^ur finite, with specialization x̄, s_{α,0} ∈ D_x̄^⊗ ⊗ Q_p denotes the φ-invariant tensors corresponding to s_{α,ét,x} under the p-adic comparison isomorphism (4.2.1). The proof of Proposition 4.2.2 shows that the same s_{α,0} correspond to s_{α,ét,x'} for every x' on the same irreducible component of Û_x̄.

items.name: Weak polarization and character-compatible twist
items.statement: An A-polarization of 𝒜 is an isomorphism 𝒜 ≅ 𝒜^* of abelian schemes up to A-isogeny, some multiple of which is a polarization. Two are equivalent if they differ by an element of A^×, and a weak A-polarization is an equivalence class. For a character c: Z → G_m, 𝒜(c) is 𝒜 with the Z-action multiplied by c, and a weak A-polarization λ is a c-polarization if the induced 𝒜 → 𝒜^*(c) is Z-equivariant. Lemma 4.4.8: there is a natural isomorphism (𝒜^*)^𝒫 ≅ (𝒜^𝒫)^*. If λ is a c-polarization, there is a unique weak A-polarization λ^𝒫: 𝒜^𝒫 → 𝒜^{𝒫*} such that, under (4.4.4) and (𝒜^*)^𝒫 ≅ 𝒜^{𝒫*}, λ^𝒫 ⊗ 1 and λ ⊗ 1 agree up to an element of O_𝒫^×.

items.name: Galois component-stabilizer extension
items.statement: §4.6.5. Fix a connected component X^+ ⊂ X; Sh(G,X)^+ ⊂ Sh(G,X) and Sh_{K_p°}(G,X)^+ ⊂ Sh_{K_p°}(G,X) are the corresponding connected Shimura varieties, and E^p ⊂ Ē is the maximal extension of E unramified at the primes dividing p. items.name: Bruhat–Tits extension criterion for smooth models
items.statement: [11, (1.7.6)]. Let 𝒢, 𝒢' be smooth affine group schemes over O with generic fibres G, G' (O^ur-points schematically dense). A K-homomorphism f: G → G' extends (uniquely) to an O-homomorphism 𝒢 → 𝒢' if and only if f(𝒢(O^ur)) ⊂ 𝒢'(O^ur). In particular, a smooth affine O-model of G is determined up to unique isomorphism by its group of O^ur-points.

items.statement: [11, (1.2.13)]. Let γ: 𝒢 → 𝒢' be a homomorphism of smooth affine O-group schemes with connected fibres which restricts to an isomorphism from an open neighbourhood of the identity section of 𝒢 (fibrewise dense, e.g. the open big cell ∏𝒰_{−a} × 𝒯 × ∏𝒰_a) onto an open subscheme of 𝒢'. Then γ is an isomorphism.
items.note: Used to show 𝒢_x°/𝒵 ≅ 𝒢̃_x̃°. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Representability of quotients over a DVR
items.statement: [1, §4] (Anantharaman). Over a Dedekind base of dimension 1 (here Spec O), the fppf quotient of a smooth affine group scheme by a flat closed normal subgroup scheme is representable by a group scheme. In the paper it is applied to 𝒢_x°/𝒵, which is then a connected smooth group scheme.
items.note: Black box. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Big-cell structure of quasi-split parahoric group schemes
items.statement: [11, (4.2.15), (4.3.2), §4.4, §4.6]. Let G be quasi-split over K (k algebraically closed), S a maximal split torus whose apartment contains x, and T = Z_G(S). The schematic closure of T in 𝒢_x° is the connected Néron model 𝒯° of T. The schematic closures 𝒰_a of the root subgroups U_a are smooth, with 𝒰_a(O) given by the valuation of root data at x. The product ∏_{a<0}𝒰_a × 𝒯° × ∏_{a>0}𝒰_a → 𝒢_x° is an open immersion (the 'open big cell'). A central isogeny/extension α with x̃ = α_*(x) induces isomorphisms 𝒰_a ≅ 𝒰̃_a. For a reductive model G_O (hyperspecial case), G_O(O^ur) is generated by 𝒯(O^ur) and the 𝒰_a(O^ur) ([11, 4.6]).
items.locator: Proof of Prop. 1.1.4 (pp. 128–129); proof of Lemma 1.2.5 (p. 132)
items.note: Black box; also used in §1.3. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Steinberg's theorem and tame cyclicity
items.statement: If k is algebraically closed, every connected reductive group over K is quasi-split (Steinberg). A tame finite Galois extension K'/K is then totally ramified with cyclic group Γ = Gal(K'/K) of order prime to p.
items.note: Classical input. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Tame fixed points of Weil restrictions are smooth; Néron models by descent
items.statement: [22, Prop. 3.1] (Edixhoven). Let K'/K be finite tame Galois with group Γ, #Γ prime to p, and X a smooth O'-scheme with a semilinear Γ-action. Then the closed fixed-point subscheme (Res_{O'/O}X)^Γ is smooth over O. For split tori 𝒯' (Néron models of T_{K'}) the neutral component of 𝒯 := (Res_{O'/O}𝒯')^Γ is the connected Néron model of T.
items.locator: Proof of Prop. 1.1.4 (finite Z case), printed p. 129; also Proof of Proposition 1.3.9, printed p. 143
items.note: The paper uses the identification of neutral components with connected Néron models without a separate citation. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Exactness of connected Néron models for tame tori
items.statement: [57, Lemma 6.7] (Pappas–Rapoport, equal characteristic; used 'by the argument in its proof' in mixed characteristic). Let 1 → T' → T → T'' → 1 be an exact sequence of tori over K, T split over a tame extension. Then there is an exact sequence of smooth O-group schemes 1 → S' → T° → T''° → 1 extending it, with T°, T''° the connected Néron models, S'° = T'°, and the component group of the special fibre of S' a subgroup of (X_*(T')_I)_tors. If X_*(T')_I is torsion-free (e.g. T' induced, or a direct summand of an induced torus), then S' = T'°.
items.locator: Proof of Prop. 1.1.4 (Z a torus), printed p. 129
items.note: I checked arXiv math/0607130, Lemma 6.7: it includes the induced-torus clause, which gives the last sentence of Prop. 1.1.4 (𝒵 = 𝒵° for direct summands of induced tori). §1.4 (1.4.9) uses that sentence. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Landvogt's canonical building map for quotient maps
items.statement: [48, Thm. 2.1.8] and its proof. For an epimorphism (in particular a central extension) a: G → G' of connected reductive groups over K there is a canonical G(K^ur)- and Gal(K^ur/K)-equivariant toral map a_*: B(G,K^ur) → B(G',K^ur); it maps hyperspecial vertices to hyperspecial vertices. For K = k((π)) (imperfect K) the proof extends when a is separable on each root subgroup.
items.note: Black box. The claim that the image of the hyperspecial x_o is hyperspecial is asserted in the proof of Prop. 1.2.3. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Landvogt: existence and uniqueness of equivariant toral embeddings
items.statement: [48, Thm. 2.2.9, Prop. 2.2.10, Prop. 2.5.2]. Let G ↪ GL(V') be a faithful representation of a connected reductive group over K. Let x ∈ B(G,K^ur) and y ∈ B(GL(V'),K^ur) satisfy Landvogt's conditions (TOR), (STAB), (CENT); for split groups (STAB) follows from Prop. 2.5.2 and (CENT) from (STAB). Then there is a unique G(K^ur)-equivariant toral isometric embedding B(G,K^ur) ↪ B(GL(V'),K^ur) with x ↦ y, and it is Galois-equivariant when y is Galois-fixed. More generally, G(K^ur)-equivariant toral maps are determined by the image of one point. Landvogt's construction also gives Galois-equivariant embeddings for non-split G (used for ι_1^L).
items.locator: §1.2.1 (p. 131); proof of Prop. 1.2.3 (p. 133); proof of Cor. 1.2.11 (p. 134); proof of Prop. 1.2.21 (p. 138); also Proof of Lemma 2.3.3, printed p. 157 (also §1.2, Prop. 1.2.21)
items.note: Black box. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Buildings of products and Levi embeddings
items.statement: [48, Prop. 2.1.6, Prop. 2.1.5]. B(∏_iG_i, K^ur) = ∏_iB(G_i,K^ur). For the Levi subgroup ∏_iGL(V_i) ⊂ GL(V), V = ⊕V_i, there is a canonical equivariant embedding ∏_iB(GL(V_i),K^ur) ↪ B(GL(V),K^ur) sending ([Λ_i ⊗ O^ur])_i to the point of the O^ur-lattice ⊕_i(Λ_i ⊗ O^ur), and more generally graded chains (c_{Λ_i} + t_i)_i as in Remark 1.2.7(c).
items.locator: Proof of Prop. 1.2.3 after (1.2.6), printed p. 133; §1.2.25, p. 138
items.note: Black box. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Translated and multi-graded toral maps; Levi factorisation
items.statement: (Remark 1.2.7, printed pp. 133–134.) (b) For t ∈ R there is a G(K^ur)-equivariant, Gal(K^ur/K)-equivariant toral map t + ι: B(G,K^ur) → B(GL(V),K^ur) determined by (t + ι)(x_o) = ({π^nΛ}_{n∈Z}, c_Λ + t) (the text misprints x_o as x). For every x, (t + ι)(x) and ι(x) have the same stabilizer in GL(V ⊗_K K^ur). (c) More generally, given for each i an O-lattice Λ_i ⊂ V_i and t_i ∈ R, with ρ_i(G_O(O^ur)) ⊂ GL(Λ_i ⊗ O^ur), the proof of Prop. 1.2.3 gives a Gal(K^ur/K)- and G(K^ur)-equivariant toral map ι (1.2.8) with ι(x_o) the image of ({π^n(Λ_i ⊗ O^ur)}_{n∈Z}, c_{Λ_i} + t_i)_i under the Levi embedding ∏_iB(GL(V_i),K^ur) ⊂ B(GL(V),K^ur). If ρ is faithful it is an isometric embedding and unique; ι(x_o) need not be hyperspecial (e.g. G_m² ↪ GL_2 over Q_p: every point of the apartment occurs). (d) In Prop. 1.2.3 and (c), ι factors through the Levi embedding determined by the decomposition of V into irreducibles; this is used in the proof of Prop. 1.3.3. In general there are equivariant maps that do not factor this way.
items.note: (b) defines the t + ι used in Cor. 1.2.11 and Prop. 1.2.21. (c) supplies the t_i of 1.2.12 and 1.3.1. (d) is used in the proof of 1.3.3. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Symplectic total lattice Λ' in V'
items.statement: (§1.1.11, last paragraph, printed p. 131.) With the chain indexed as in (1.1.12), let V' := ⊕_{i=−(r−1)−a}^{r−1} V with the perfect alternating form ψ' := ⊥_{i} ψ (orthogonal direct sum), so there is a diagonal embedding GSp(V,ψ) ↪ GSp(V',ψ') ⊂ GL(V'). Set Λ' := ⊕_{i=−(r−1)−a}^{r−1} Λ^i ⊂ V'. Then 𝒢𝒮𝒫_x is the schematic closure of GSp(V,ψ) in GL(Λ'). After replacing Λ' by a scalar multiple, ψ' is integral on Λ', i.e. Λ' ⊂ Λ'^∨ (dual for ψ').
items.note: Reused verbatim in §2.3.15 (V'_{Z_p} ⊂ V'^∨_{Z_p}). Correct: ∏_iGL(Λ^i) is closed (block diagonal) in GL(Λ'). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Twisted-form presentation of a tamely split group
items.statement: (§1.2.14, printed pp. 135–136.) Let G split over a tamely ramified Galois extension K̃/K, Γ = Gal(K̃/K) (K̃/K possibly infinite, inertia subgroup of Γ finite). Choose ψ: G ⊗_K K̃ ≅ H ⊗_{Z_p} K̃ (H the pinned Chevalley form) and write G(K) = H(K̃)^Γ for the action γ·h̃ = c(γ)·γ(h̃), where c: Γ → Aut(H)(K̃), c(γ) = ψ·γ(ψ)^{−1}, is a cocycle representing the class of G in H^1(Γ, Aut(H)(K̃)). The pinning gives Aut(H)(K̃) = H^ad(K̃) ⋊ Ξ with Ξ the pinning-preserving automorphisms. Under tameness, B(G,K) = B(G,K̃)^Γ = B(H,K̃)^Γ, with Γ acting on B(H,K̃) through the twisted action on H(K̃).
items.note: Sets up the cocycle c used in (1.2.20) and in §1.3/§2. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Tame Galois descent of buildings
items.statement: (Rousseau; Prasad–Yu [60].) If G splits over a tamely ramified Galois extension K̃/K with group Γ (finite inertia), the canonical map B(G,K) ↪ B(G,K̃) identifies B(G,K) with B(G,K̃)^Γ. Similarly, for the inertia subgroup I_1 ⊂ Γ_1, B(G,K̃)^{I_1} = B(G,K̃^{I_1}), and B(GL(V(λ_1)),K̃)^{I_1} for the c'-twisted action is B(GL(V)_D, K_1^ur).
items.note: Black box. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Tits' description of irreducible representations over non-closed fields
items.statement: [69, 3.1, Thm. 3.3, proof of Thm. 7.6], [66]. For G reductive over K (char 0) split over K̃ and ρ: G → GL(V) irreducible over K: Γ acts on dominant weights; V ⊗_K K̃ = ⊕_{i=1}^r V_{λ_i,K̃} with Γ permuting summands transitively compatibly with {λ_i}; V_{λ_i,K̃} ≃ V(λ_i)^{⊕d} ⊗_{Q_p} K̃ with d independent of i; the centralizer D^0 is a division algebra whose centre (that of D = (D^0)^opp) is K_1 = K̃^{Stab(λ_1)}; and ρ = Res_{K_1/K}(Res_{D/K_1} ∘ ρ̄_1) for an absolutely irreducible ρ̄_1 obtained by descending the Weyl module ρ_1 via c' = θ∘c.
items.note: Black box underlying R05. The paper writes 'As in loc. cit.' for each step. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Weights of minuscule representations
items.statement: [7, Ch. VIII, §7, 3] (Bourbaki). If ρ is an irreducible minuscule representation of a split reductive group with maximal split torus T, then its set of weights W(ρ) ⊂ X^•(T) is a single Weyl orbit W·λ_0 of the highest weight, and every weight space V_λ is one-dimensional.
items.locator: Proof of Prop. 1.2.10, printed p. 134 (again in Prop. 1.3.3)
items.note: Black box. R02 records the modular consequence ([41, II 2.15]). Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Reduction of Proposition 1.3.3 to smoothness of a schematic closure
items.statement: Let y = ι(x) with periodic lattice chain Λ^•_y = {Λ^i_y}. Since ι is injective and G(K^ur)-equivariant, G(K^ur)_x = G(K^ur) ∩ GL(V ⊗ K^ur)_y ⊂ GL(Λ^•_y ⊗ O^ur), and [11, (1.7.6)] gives a homomorphism ρ: 𝒢_x → 𝒢ℒ_y. Let 𝒢'_x be the schematic closure of G in 𝒢ℒ_y, which equals the scheme-theoretic image of ρ. Then 𝒢'_x(O^ur) = 𝒢_x(O^ur), and ρ is a closed immersion as soon as 𝒢'_x is smooth. By §1.1.9 this is equivalent to smoothness of the schematic closure of the diagonal G ⊂ Π_{i=0}^{r-1} GL(V) in Π_{i=0}^{r-1} GL(Λ^i_y).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 1.3.3, opening paragraph, printed pp. 139–140
items.note: Reused in the proof of Prop. 2.3.7 (C's range). The index r here (period of the chain) clashes with r = rank of T in step 1); harmless. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The lattice chain at ι(x) splits into weight lines
items.statement: Let G be split over K, T ≅ G_m^r a maximal split torus with x ∈ A(G,T,K), and ρ = ⊕_j ρ_j: G → GL(V) = GL(⊕_j V_j) faithful with each V_j irreducible and minuscule. Let y = ι(x) for the Levi-type map ι of (1.2.13)/§1.2.25 (with translations t_j). Then for every i, Λ^i_y = ⊕_j ⊕_{λ ∈ W(ρ_j)} Λ^i_{j,λ,y} (1.3.6), with Λ^i_{j,λ,y} ⊂ V_{j,λ} a rank-one O-lattice. In particular (irreducible case (1.3.5)) y lies in the apartment A(GL(V), T^♭, K) of the torus T^♭ = Π_λ GL(V_λ).
items.note: Uses that the closure 𝒯 ≅ G^r_{m/O} of T in 𝒢_x acts on each Λ^i_y, that minuscule weight spaces are lines ([7, VIII §7.3]), and, for several V_j, the Levi factorization of ι (1.2.3, 1.2.25, Remark 1.2.7(d)). Remark 1.3.7 explains why the splitting fails without minusculity. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Big-cell smoothness criterion for schematic closures (Bruhat–Tits II, 2.2.3 and 2.2.5; cited)
items.statement: Let G be split reductive over K with split maximal torus T and root groups U_a, and let 𝒢' be the schematic closure of G in a smooth affine O-group scheme (here Π_i GL(Λ^i_y)). If the schematic closures 𝒯 of T and 𝒰_a of the U_a in it are smooth, then 𝒢' contains Π_{a<0} 𝒰_a × 𝒯 × Π_{a>0} 𝒰_a as a smooth open big cell ([11, Thm. 2.2.3]), and 𝒢' is smooth ([11, Cor. 2.2.5]).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 1.3.3, step 1), printed p. 142, citing [11] = Bruhat–Tits, Publ. IHÉS 60 (1984)
items.note: Black box. Statement paraphrased from its use; the exact hypotheses of BT II §2.2 (schematic root data) should be checked when implementing. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Root-group closures for lattices in a common apartment are smooth (Bruhat–Tits [12], 3.6 and 3.9(2); cited)
items.statement: Let SL_2 act on standard representations V_{j,[λ]} with bases e_{j,λ}, f_{j,λ} = X_a e_{j,λ}. Let Λ^i_{j,[λ],y} = π^{n_{j,[λ],i}} O e_{j,λ} ⊕ π^{m_{j,[λ],i}} O f_{j,λ}, all in the standard apartment of the chosen basis. Then the schematic closures of U_± ⊂ SL_2 in Π_{j,[λ]} Π_i GL(Λ^i_{j,[λ],y}) are smooth. Consequently the closures 𝒰_{±a} of U_{±a} in Π_i GL(Λ^i_y) are smooth, and so is the closure of T.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 1.3.3, step 1), printed pp. 141–142
items.note: Black box ([12] = Bruhat–Tits, Bull. SMF 112 (1984)). It is also directly checkable: the closure of u ↦ (1 u; 0 1) in the product is Spec O[π^{-c}u] ≅ G_{a,O}, where c = max_i(m_i − n_i). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Smoothness of a torus closure with maximal bounded integral points (Prasad–Yu [61, Lemma 4.1]; cited)
items.statement: Let G be split over K (not necessarily semisimple), x ∈ A(G,T,K) and y = ι(x). The O^ur-points of the Zariski closure 𝒯 of T in 𝒢ℒ_y form the maximal bounded subgroup of T(K^ur), because Aut(Λ^•_y) ∩ G(K^ur) = G(K^ur)_x contains it. Hence 𝒯 is smooth by [61, Lemma 4.1]. The unipotent closures 𝒰_a are the same for G and G^der, so step 1) applies.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 1.3.3, step 2), printed p. 142
items.note: Black box: [61] = Prasad–Yu, J. Algebraic Geom. 15 (2006). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Comparison of ι with the split-field Levi maps (1.3.11)–(1.3.12)
items.statement: The embedding ι of (1.3.2) sits in a commutative diagram (1.3.11): B(G,K) → Π_j B(Res_{K_{j1}/K} GL(V_j)_{D_j}, K) → B(GL(V),K), over B(G,K̃) → Π_j B(Res_{K_{j1}/K} GL(V_j)_{D_j} ⊗_K K̃, K̃), with the natural vertical embeddings. The top arrow is the G(K̃)-map (ι_{j,σ})_{j,σ} attached to the faithful representation ρ'_{K̃}: G_{K̃} → Π_j Π_σ GL(V(λ_{j1}) ⊗_{Q_p} K̃), a sum of minuscule irreducible representations of the split group G_{K̃} (σ over K-embeddings K_{j1} → K̃). The split case gives the closed immersion (1.3.12) 𝒢_{x,K̃} ↪ Π_j Π_σ 𝒢ℒ(V(λ_j) ⊗_{Q_p} K̃)_{ι_{j,σ}(x)}.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 1.3.3, step 3), (1.3.11)–(1.3.12), printed p. 143
items.note: Combined with (1.3.10) and [12, 3.5, 3.9] (the restriction-of-scalars map Res_{O_{j1}/O}((𝒢ℒ(V_j)_{D_j})_{ι_j(x)}) → 𝒢ℒ(V_j)_{ι_j(x)} is a closed immersion, cf. (1.2.19)), this gives the tame case of Prop. 1.3.3. (1.3.12) writes V(λ_j) where the display above has V(λ_{j1}); harmless. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Serre's Conjecture II for quasi-split groups without E8 factors (Gille [28]; cited)
items.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic 0 with cd(F) ≤ 2, and H a semisimple simply connected quasi-split group over F with no factors of type E8. Then H^1(F, H) = 1.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 1.4.6, printed p. 145, citing [28] = Gille, Compos. Math. 125 (2001)
items.note: Black box, applied to 𝒦 = Frac(W(k)[[u]]), which has cd 2 only for k algebraically closed (see U04 and the source issue on Lemma 1.4.6). The paper also points to Bayer-Fluckiger–Parimala [2], [3] for classical groups. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Parahoric lift of the flasque resolution and the H^2 obstruction (1.4.9)
items.statement: Assume k is algebraically closed, G is tame with no E8 factors, 1 → Z → G̃ → G → 1 is the flasque resolution (1.4.7) with Z a direct summand of an induced torus, and x̄ ∈ B(G^ad,K_0) = B(G̃^ad,K_0) is the image of x. Proposition 1.1.4 gives an fppf-exact sequence of smooth W-group schemes 1 → 𝒵° → 𝒢̃ → 𝒢 → 1, with 𝒵° the connected Néron model of Z and 𝒢̃ = 𝒢̃°_{x̄}. Since H^1(D[1/p], G̃) = 1 by Lemmas 1.4.5 and 1.4.6, 𝒥[1/p] is trivial iff its image in H^2(D[1/p], Z) vanishes. That image equals the image of 𝒥 under H^1(D×,𝒢) → H^2(D×,𝒵°) → H^2(D[1/p],Z), which is trivial by Lemma 1.4.5.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 1.4.3, Step 2, (1.4.9), printed p. 146
items.note: Uses that the connected Néron model of Z ×_{K_0} Z' ≅ Q' is 𝒵° × 𝒵'°, so the H^2 image for Z is a direct summand of that for Q'. The paper also records that the centralizer tori T̃ of G̃ and G̃^der are induced (used in Step 3). Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Rank-one parahoric cosets over O_ℰ and W[[u]] (1.4.10)–(1.4.12)
items.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, 𝒢 = ℐ an Iwahori group scheme, s_i (i = 1..m) the simple affine reflections of the alcove, and 𝒢_i ⊃ 𝒢 the parahorics with 𝒢_i(W) = 𝒢(W) ⊔ 𝒢(W)s_i𝒢(W). Let G_i be the maximal reductive quotient of 𝒢_i ⊗_W k (derived group SL_2 or PSL_2) and B_i ⊂ G_i the Borel with 𝒢(O_ℰ) = q_i^{-1}(B_i(k((u)))). Reduction mod p gives surjections q_i: 𝒢_i(O_ℰ) → G_i(k((u))) and 𝒢_i(W[[u]]) → G_i(k[[u]]). These induce bijections 𝒢_i(O_ℰ)/𝒢(O_ℰ) ≅ G_i(k((u)))/B_i(k((u))) ≅ P^1(k((u))) (1.4.10) and 𝒢_i(W[[u]])/𝒢(W[[u]]) ≅ P^1(k[[u]]) (1.4.11), compatible along W[[u]] → O_ℰ. Since P^1(k[[u]]) = P^1(k((u))), 𝒢_i(O_ℰ) = 𝒢_i(W[[u]])·𝒢(O_ℰ) (1.4.12).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 1.4.3, Step 3, (1.4.10)–(1.4.12), printed pp. 147–148
items.note: Also uses the reduction to 𝒢 = ℐ: ℐ(O_ℰ) ⊂ 𝒢(O_ℰ) for an Iwahori ℐ whose alcove contains x in its closure. Surjectivity of 𝒢̄_i(k((u))) → G_i(k((u))) uses that the unipotent radical is split (k perfect). 'G_i^red' on p. 147 means G_i^der. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: G(ℰ)^1 lies in G(W[[u]][1/p])·𝒢(O_ℰ)
items.statement: For n ≥ 1 and i_1, …, i_n ∈ [1,m], every coset y_1⋯y_n·𝒢(O_ℰ) with y_k ∈ 𝒢_{i_k}(O_ℰ) equals g_1⋯g_n·𝒢(O_ℰ) with g_k ∈ 𝒢_{i_k}(W[[u]]) ⊂ G(W[[u]][1/p]). This follows by applying (1.4.12) inductively to the action of 𝒢(O_ℰ)^n. Hence, writing G(ℰ)^1 for the subgroup of G(ℰ) generated by the 𝒢_i(O_ℰ), the image of G(W[[u]][1/p]) in G(ℰ)/𝒢(O_ℰ) contains G(ℰ)^1/𝒢(O_ℰ).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 1.4.3, Step 3, printed p. 148
items.note: Proof step of U09. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: G(ℰ) = T(K_0)·G(ℰ)^1 (1.4.13)–(1.4.14)
items.statement: With k algebraically closed, S ⊂ G a maximal split torus whose apartment contains x, T = Z_G(S) and 𝒯 its closure in 𝒢_x: G(ℰ)^1 coincides with the subgroup generated by all parahoric subgroups of G(ℰ) ([11, 5.2.11]) and with the subgroup generated by 𝒯°(O_ℰ) and the U_a(ℰ) ([11, 5.2.4]). Hence G(ℰ) = T(ℰ)·G(ℰ)^1 (1.4.13). The map T(K_0)/𝒯°(W) → T(ℰ)/𝒯°(O_ℰ) is surjective: for induced T by [11, 4.4.14]; in general write T = T̃/Z with T̃ induced and Z a direct summand of an induced torus, so H^1(ℰ,Z) = 1 and T̃(ℰ) → T(ℰ) is onto. Therefore G(ℰ) = T(K_0)·G(ℰ)^1 (1.4.14). Since T(K_0) ⊂ G(W[[u]][1/p]), this proves U09.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 1.4.3, Step 3, (1.4.13)–(1.4.14), printed p. 148
items.note: Applies Bruhat–Tits theory to G over ℰ, whose residue field k((u)) is imperfect, and identifies the 𝒢_i ⊗_W O_ℰ with its parahorics; see the gap recorded in sourceIssues. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Gluing sections along D[1/p] ⊔ Spec O_ℰ → D× (Grothendieck fpqc descent; Gille [29, Appendix]; cited)
items.statement: D[1/p] ⊔ Spec(O_ℰ) → D× is an fpqc covering. If a 𝒢-torsor 𝒥 over D× has sections a[1/p] over D[1/p] and a_p over O_ℰ that agree on Spec ℰ, then they glue to a section over D×, so 𝒥 is trivial. In Step 3 the agreement is arranged by modifying the sections using G(ℰ) = G(W[[u]][1/p])·𝒢(O_ℰ).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 1.4.3, Step 3, printed pp. 146–147, citing [6, Ch. 6, Thm. 6(a)] and [29, Appendix]
items.note: Black box. The descent condition over O_ℰ ⊗_{D×} O_ℰ follows from agreement over Spec ℰ, because O_ℰ ⊗ O_ℰ is p-torsion-free and 𝒥 is affine. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: The minuscule Schubert variety S_μ is the flag variety X_μ
items.statement: Let μ be minuscule (⟨a,μ⟩ ∈ {−1,0,1} for all roots a) with reflex field E. G_{Q̄_p}/P_{μ^{-1}} has a canonical model X_μ over E; if G is quasi-split, {μ} has a representative μ defined over E ([45, 1.1.3]) and X_μ = G_E/P_{μ^{-1}}. The affine Schubert variety S_μ(Q̄_p) = G(Q̄_p[[t]])μ(t)G(Q̄_p[[t]])/G(Q̄_p[[t]]) is closed in Gr_{G,K} ×_K Q̄_p ([58, p. 146]). It is Gal(Q̄_p/E)-stable, so it descends to a closed S_μ ⊂ Gr_{G,K} ×_K E. The stabilizer H_μ = G(Q̄_p[[t]]) ∩ μ(t)G(Q̄_p[[t]])μ(t)^{-1} contains T(Q̄_p[[t]]) and ker(G(Q̄_p[[t]]) → G(Q̄_p)), and its image in G(Q̄_p) is P_{μ^{-1}}(Q̄_p). Hence S_μ ≅ X_μ G_E-equivariantly.
items.note: This identification is how X_μ sits inside the global Grassmannian in the definition of M^loc (M02). Black boxes: [45, 1.1.3], [58, p. 146]. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Normality from a normal generic fibre and a reduced special fibre (as in [59, Prop. 9.2]; cited)
items.statement: Let X be a flat O_L-scheme of finite type whose generic fibre is normal and whose special fibre is reduced. Then X is normal. Applied to M^loc ⊗_{O_E} O_L, whose special fibre is reduced by Theorem 2.1.2 and whose generic fibre X_μ ⊗_E L is smooth, this gives Corollary 2.1.3.
items.note: Black box, invoked as 'follows as in [59, Prop. 9.2]'. It is elementary: an element a/π^n integral over X forces a^m ∈ πA, so a ∈ πA because A/π is reduced. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Explicit construction of G̲ and 𝒢̲ for quasi-split G (2.1.5)–(2.1.6)
items.statement: Let G/K be quasi-split, split over a tame finite Galois K̃/K with Γ = Gal(K̃/K). Choose a maximal split torus S, T = Z_G(S), a Borel B ⊃ S with based root datum R^+, the split Chevalley form H over Z_p with pinning (T_H, B_H, e), and Ξ = Aut(R^+) (the pinned automorphisms of H). G corresponds to ξ: Gal(Q̄_p/K) → Ξ factoring through Γ, and hence to ξ̲: π_1(Spec O[u^{±1}]) → Ξ (u ↦ p). Then ψ: G ≅ (Res_{K̃/K}(H ⊗ K̃))^Γ with γ acting by ξ(γ) ⊗ γ (2.1.5), and G̲ := (Res_{O_0[v^{±1}]/O[u^{±1}]}(H ⊗_{O[u^{±1}]} O_0[v^{±1}]))^Γ (2.1.6), where O_0[v^{±1}]/O[u^{±1}] is the Γ-cover of [59, 3.2] specializing to K̃/K at u = p. For x ∈ A(G,S,K), [59, Thm. 4.1] gives a smooth affine 𝒢̲ over O[u] extending G̲ with 𝒢̲ ⊗_{u↦p} O = 𝒢. For κ = K or k, [59, 4.1] identifies A(G,S,K) with an apartment of B(G̲_{κ((u))}, κ((u))) (κ((u)) valued by u), and 𝒢̲ ⊗_{O[u]} κ[[u]] is the parahoric group scheme of the point x_{κ((u))} corresponding to x.
items.note: Used later in §2.3 ('see 2.1.4', printed pp. ~160–163) and §4.7. By Steinberg's theorem G becomes quasi-split after enlarging the unramified K/Q_p. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: The adjoint morphism of local models ad_* (§2.2.3)
items.statement: Let G/Q_p split over a tame extension, ad: G → G^ad, x ∈ B(G,Q_p), x̄ = ad_*(x) ∈ B(G^ad,Q_p), and E_ad ⊂ E the reflex field of {μ_ad}. Proposition 2.2.2 applied to ad gives Gr_{𝒢̲,X} → Gr_{𝒢̲^ad,X}. This induces a morphism ad_*: M^loc_{G,{μ},x} → M^loc_{G^ad,{μ_ad},x̄} ⊗_{O_{E_ad}} O_E, equivariant for ad: 𝒢 → 𝒢^ad; here 𝒢, 𝒢^ad, 𝒢^der denote the parahoric group schemes attached to x̄.
items.note: Source of the morphism in M07 (Prop. 2.2.4). Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Special-fibre description and quasi-finiteness of ad_* ⊗ k ([59, Cor. 6.6], [57, §6]; cited)
items.statement: By [59, Cor. 6.6], ad_* ⊗_{O_E} k is the restriction of the natural morphism Gr_{P_k} → Gr_{P^ad_k}, where P_k = 𝒢̲ ⊗_{Z_p[u]} k[[u]] and P^ad_k = 𝒢̲^ad ⊗_{Z_p[u]} k[[u]]. On each connected component of Gr_{P_k} this morphism is finite-to-one on k-points ([57, §6(a),(b)], proof of (6.19)). Hence ad_* ⊗ k is quasi-finite. With normality of source and target and Zariski's main theorem, this makes ad_*^~ an isomorphism.
items.note: Black boxes; k must be read as an algebraic closure of the residue field for 'finite-to-one on k-points' to give quasi-finiteness. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Derived parahorics under a central isogeny (2.2.6)
items.statement: In the situation of §2.2.5, with (a) a central isogeny α: G^der → G'^der inducing (G^ad,{μ_ad}) ≅ (G'^ad,{μ'_ad}), (b) x, x' mapping to the same x̄ ∈ B(G^ad,Q_p), and (c) p ∤ |π_1(G'^der)|: the kernel C of α is finite of order prime to p, and E_ad ⊂ E, E'. α extends to 𝒢^der → 𝒢'^der, 𝒢^ad = 𝒢'^ad, and by Proposition 1.1.4, 𝒢'^der ≅ 𝒢^der/𝒞, where 𝒞 is the smooth schematic closure of C in 𝒢^der and the isomorphism is induced by α.
items.note: The data (a)–(c) are the hypotheses of Prop. 2.2.7 (M08). (2.2.6) is not cited again explicitly, but the equivariance statement of Prop. 2.2.7 refers to α: 𝒢^der → 𝒢'^der. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Local Hodge embedding
items.statement: Let K = Q_p and (G,{μ},K) be as in §2.1.1. A (local) Hodge embedding is a faithful symplectic representation ρ: G → GSp(V) ⊂ GL(V) such that ρ∘μ is conjugate to the minuscule coweight μ_0 of GSp(V), a ↦ diag(a^{(g)}, 1^{(g)}) (dim V = 2g), ρ is minuscule (cf. [20, table 1.3.9]), and G ⊂ GL(V) contains the torus G_m of scalars.
items.note: Used in Lemma 2.3.3, Prop. 2.3.7, Cor. 2.3.16 and later in §§3–4; no existing item in any range defines it. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Data of §2.3.1 and the toral embeddings ι and s
items.statement: Choose a Q_p-split torus A with x ∈ A(G,A,Q_p) and a maximal Q_p^ur-split torus S ⊃ A defined over Q_p ([11, 5.1.12]); T = Z_G(S) is a maximal torus defined over Q_p and split over K̃. Choose a pinning (T_H,B_H,e) of the split Chevalley form H of G over Z_p and ψ: G_K̃ ≅ H_K̃ with ψ(T_K̃) = (T_H)_K̃ and ψ^{−1}((B_H)_K̃) defined over Q_p^ur; after composing ψ with conjugation by an element of T_{H^ad}(K̃), c(γ) = ψ·γ(ψ)^{−1} preserves the pinning for γ in the inertia I_K̃ = Gal(K̃/(K̃∩Q_p^ur)). These choices, with irreducible summands V_j, highest weight vectors v_1 and translations t ∈ R, give by §1.2 a G(Q_p^ur)- and Gal(Q_p^ur/Q_p)-equivariant toral embedding ι: B(G,Q_p^ur) → B(GL(V),Q_p^ur) (2.3.2). There is also a canonical equivariant toral embedding s: B(GSp(V),Q_p^ur) → B(GL(V),Q_p^ur).
items.note: 'The above data' in Lemma 2.3.3 refers to exactly these choices. The text says ι was 'constructed in the previous paragraph', meaning §1.2 (1.2.26). Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Closed immersions 𝒢_x → 𝒢𝒮𝒫_z → 𝒢ℒ_y
items.statement: With data as in Lemma 2.3.3, let x ∈ B(G,Q_p), z = j(x), y = ι(x) = s(z), and 𝒢𝒮𝒫_z the parahoric group scheme of GSp(V) at z. The periodic lattice chain Λ_y^• is self-dual, and ρ extends to affine smooth group scheme homomorphisms ρ: 𝒢_x → 𝒢𝒮𝒫_z → 𝒢ℒ_y (2.3.5). By Proposition 1.3.3, 𝒢_x → 𝒢ℒ_y is a closed immersion, and hence so is 𝒢_x → 𝒢𝒮𝒫_z.
items.note: 𝒢_x is the Bruhat–Tits stabilizer group scheme (1.1.2), as in Prop. 1.3.3. Used in §2.3.15 and later. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Symplectic lattice-chain local model and the embedding (2.3.6) (cited)
items.statement: The local model M^loc_GSp := M^loc_{GSp(V),{μ_0},z}, for GSp(V), its standard minuscule coweight μ_0 and the periodic self-dual lattice chain Λ_z^•, was considered by Görtz [31] and agrees with the corresponding local model of [59]. Its generic fibre over Q_p is the Lagrangian Grassmannian LGr(V) of maximal isotropic subspaces of V. The standard embedding 𝒢𝒮𝒫_z → 𝒢ℒ_y induces a closed immersion M^loc_GSp ↪ M^loc_{GL(V),{μ_0},y}. Since ρ∘μ is conjugate to μ_0, ρ induces a closed immersion X_μ ↪ LGr(V) ⊗_{Q_p} E (2.3.6).
items.note: Black-box inputs: Görtz's flatness of the symplectic local model and its identification with the Pappas–Zhu local model. Needed to read Prop. 2.3.7 (target and the reduction to (2.3.9)). Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Pappas–Zhu criterion for closed immersions of local models (cited)
items.statement: ([59, Prop. 8.1, 8.1.1], in its GL-variant.) Let L = Q_p^ur, O = O_L with residue field k. If ρ_L: G_L ↪ GL(V_L) extends to a group scheme homomorphism ρ̲_{O[u]}: 𝒢̲ → GL(N_•) over Spec O[u], for some periodic O[u]-lattice chain N_•, satisfying (*): the Zariski closure of 𝒢̲ ⊗_{O[u]} k((u)) in GL(N_• ⊗_{O[u]} k[[u]]) is a smooth group scheme which stabilizes x_{k((u))}, and ρ̲_{O[u]} ⊗ k[[u]] identifies 𝒢̲ ⊗_{O[u]} k[[u]] = 𝒢°_{x_{k((u))}} with the neutral component of that closure; then ρ̲_{O[u]} induces a closed immersion of local models M^loc_{G_L,{μ},x} ↪ M^loc_{GL(V),{μ_0},y} ⊗ O_{E'}.
items.note: The paper notes that [59, 8.1] treats GSp-type targets and says 'the argument is the same' for GL. The printed (*) has k((u)) where k[[u]] is meant (see sourceIssues). Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Projective modules over O[v] are free (cited)
items.statement: ([68]) Finitely generated projective modules over the polynomial ring O[v] over the discrete valuation ring O are free.
items.locator: Proof of Prop. 2.3.7, Step 1, printed p. 160
items.note: Used to see that (ℒ_j ⊗_O O[w])^{I_{j1}} and its weight-orbit summands are O[v]-free. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Satake's structure theorem for symplectic representations (cited)
items.statement: ([66, Theorem 1 and §2.1]) The Q_p-primary summands of V are of type (a) W^∨ ≅ W, (b) W^∨ ≅ σ(W) for some σ, or (c) W^∨ ≇ σ(W) for all σ (W a geometrically irreducible G_1-summand), and one reduces to V Q_p-primary of type (a)/(b) or V = V_a ⊕ V_a^∨ with V_a of type (c). If V = V'^{⊕m} is of type (a) with V' Q_p-irreducible, there are a field K_1/K, a central division K_1-algebra D with involution of the first kind, a right D-module V'_1 and a left D-module V_2 with m = dim_D V_2, and non-degenerate ε-hermitian h_1 on V'_1 and (−ε)-hermitian h_2 on V_2, such that ρ|_{G_1} is the composite of G_1 → Res_{K_1/K}(G_{1,K_1}), the restriction of scalars of G_{1,K_1} →^{(ρ_1,1)} U(V'_1/D,h_1) × U(D\V_2,h_2) →^{⊗} Sp(V_1), and Res_{K_1/K}Sp(V_1) → Sp(V); here V_1 = V'_1 ⊗_D V_2 is V with its K_1-structure, with alternating form the D/K_1-trace of h_1 ⊗ ^t h_2.
items.note: Black box for Lemma 2.3.3 only. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Normal decomposition and M̃_1
items.statement: Let M be a free Ŵ(R)-module and M_1 ⊂ M a submodule with I_R M ⊂ M_1 and M/M_1 projective over R (e.g. from a Dieudonné display). A normal decomposition is a decomposition M = L ⊕ T into Ŵ(R)-submodules with M_1 = L ⊕ I_R T; condition (ii) implies one exists. M̃_1 is the image of φ*(i): φ*M_1 = Ŵ(R) ⊗_{φ,Ŵ(R)} M_1 → φ*M = Ŵ(R) ⊗_{φ,Ŵ(R)} M induced by the inclusion i: M_1 → M. M̃_1 and the notion of normal decomposition depend only on (M,M_1), not on Φ, Φ_1.
items.note: Used in Lemmas 3.1.5, 3.1.9, 3.1.12 and in §3.2. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Base change of Dieudonné displays; deformations
items.statement: Let R → R' be a morphism of complete local rings with residue field k and (M,M_1,Φ,Φ_1) a Dieudonné display over R. Its base change to R' ([75, Defn. 20]) is M_{R'} = M ⊗_{Ŵ(R)} Ŵ(R'), M_{R',1} = ker(M_{R'} → M/M_1 ⊗_R R') = Im(M_1 ⊗_{Ŵ(R)} Ŵ(R') → M_{R'}) + I_{R'}M_{R'}, Φ the φ-semilinear extension of Φ, and Φ_1 the unique φ-semilinear map M_{R',1} → M_{R'} with Φ_1(w ⊗ m_1) = φ(w) ⊗ Φ_1(m_1) (w ∈ Ŵ(R'), m_1 ∈ M_1) and Φ_1(V(w) ⊗ m) = w ⊗ Φ(m) (w ∈ Ŵ(R'), m ∈ M); existence and uniqueness follow from a normal decomposition. If R → R' is surjective, a deformation to R of a display over R' is a display over R with an identification of its base change with the given display.
items.note: D04 records only the compatibility with M̃_1. The construction and the notion of deformation (used in §3.1.7, Lemmas 3.1.12 and 3.1.17, §3.2) have no item. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Lemma 3.1.9 as printed (first-order comparison of M̃_1 with D̃_1)
items.statement: Let a_R = m_R^2 + pR. There is a canonical commutative diagram with top row M̃_1 ⊗_{Ŵ(R)} Ŵ(R/a_R) → φ*(M_{R/a_R}), bottom row D̃_1 ⊗_W Ŵ(R/a_R) → φ*(D) ⊗_W Ŵ(R/a_R), left vertical arrow an isomorphism (from bottom-left to top-left, printed as a downward ≅) and right vertical arrow the identity, where the horizontal maps are induced by the natural inclusions M̃_1 → φ*(M_R) and D̃_1 → φ*(D).
items.note: Defective as printed: the isomorphism built in the proof depends on the normal decomposition, and the diagram does not determine it (E1). It is replaced by KPZ26 Lemma 5.1.15 (the extraction's D07). Record the printed statement so that E1 and §3.1.11 have a target. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Ψ constant modulo a_R
items.statement: In the situation of §3.1.8, Ψ is constant modulo a_R if the composite D̃_1 ⊗_W Ŵ(R/a_R) ≅ M̃_1 ⊗_{Ŵ(R)} Ŵ(R/a_R) →^Ψ M_{R/a_R} ≅ D ⊗_W Ŵ(R/a_R) equals Ψ_0 ⊗ 1, the first isomorphism being that of Lemma 3.1.9.
items.note: Hypothesis of Lemma 3.1.12 and standing assumption from §3.1.14 on. Not well defined as printed (E1). KPZ26 §5.1.19 redefines it with c of KPZ26 Lemma 5.1.15. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Extension of Φ_1 over a divided-power thickening (cited)
items.statement: ([73, Thm. 3], as used in the proof of Lemma 3.1.12) Regard R/a_R → k as a thickening with trivial divided powers on m_R/a_R. For a Dieudonné display (M,M_1,Φ,Φ_1) over R/a_R, Φ_1 extends uniquely to a φ-semilinear map Φ̂_1: M̂_1 → M, where M̂_1 = M_1 + W(m_R/a_R)M (3.1.13).
items.note: Exact hypotheses of [73, Thm. 3] not checked against Zink. The statement records what KP18 uses. It may fall under FOUND P08 if that carrier covers Zink's display version. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Deformations of Dieudonné displays along divided-power thickenings (cited)
items.statement: ([73, Thm. 4], as used in the proof of Lemma 3.1.12) For a divided-power thickening such as R/a_R → k with trivial divided powers, the Dieudonné displays over R/a_R lifting a given display over k correspond bijectively to lifts of its Hodge filtration; the correspondence is through the extended map Φ̂_1 on M̂_1 of [73, Thm. 3], which depends only on the display over k.
items.note: Grothendieck–Messing theorem for displays. Exact form of [73, Thm. 4] not checked against Zink. Possibly covered by FOUND P08. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Def(𝒢_S; S'), Def(f; S') and dual numbers
items.statement: From §3.1.14 on, Ψ is assumed constant mod a_R, so 𝒢_R (equivalently M = M_R) is versal. For a surjection S' → S of W-algebras and a p-divisible group 𝒢_S over S, Def(𝒢_S; S') is the set of isomorphism classes of deformations of 𝒢_S to S'; when S' → S has nilpotent kernel such deformations have no automorphisms. For a map f: A → S of W-algebras, Def(f; S') is the set of lifts of f to maps A → S'. For any ring A, A[ε] = A[X]/X^2.
items.note: Used in Lemma 3.1.15 and in §3.2. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Breuil's comparison for p-divisible groups over O_K (cited)
items.statement: ([8, Prop. 5.1.3], as used in §3.1.18) For K/K_0 finite and totally ramified with uniformizer π and Eisenstein polynomial E(u), and S the p-adic completion of W[u, E(u)^i/i!]_{i≥1}, the weakly admissible filtered φ-module of a p-divisible group over O_K is obtained from the evaluation of its Dieudonné crystal on S (Frobenius via S → W, filtration via u ↦ π). Composed with S → Ŵ(O_K), u ↦ [π], this identifies it with the filtered φ-module of §3.1.18.
items.note: Exact content of Breuil's Prop. 5.1.3 not checked. FOUND P09 (Breuil–Kisin integral comparison) is a different input. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: G-splitting of filtrations on weakly admissible modules (cited, [43, Lemma 1.4.5])
items.statement: Let D be a weakly admissible filtered φ-module over K_0, with filtration on D_K = D⊗_{K_0}K, and let (s_α) ⊂ Fil^0 D^⊗ be φ-invariant tensors defining a reductive subgroup G ⊂ GL(D). Then the filtration on D_K is G_K-split, i.e. induced by a G-valued cocharacter defined over K. Footnote 4 corrects the last line of the proof. Aut^⊗(ω) of the Tannakian category ⟨D⟩^⊗ generated by D need not be reductive, so (1.1.3) cannot be applied to it. Instead, the filtration on ⟨D⟩^⊗⊗K induces one on the category ⟨D⟩^{⊗,G} generated by the G-representation D, and (1.1.3) applies there.
items.locator: §3.2.5 and footnote 4, printed pp. 170–171; used again in the proof of Lemma 3.2.6, printed p. 171. [43] = Kisin, JAMS 23 (2010), Lemma (1.4.5)
items.note: Black box behind μ_y and μ. I checked the hypothesis wording (D weakly admissible) in Kisin's corrected version on his homepage (shimcorrpub.dvi, 2024), which already contains the footnote-4 argument. §3.2.5 does not check weak admissibility; see the new gap. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Component-group sequence; reduction of the tensor torsor to 𝒢°
items.statement: (3.2.7) There is an exact sequence of étale sheaves on Spec W, 1 → 𝒢° → 𝒢 → i_*(Γ) → 1, with Γ finite constant on Spec k and i: Spec k ↪ Spec W. Hence (3.2.8) there is an exact sequence of pointed sets H^1(D^×,𝒢°) → H^1(D^×,𝒢) → H^1(D^×⊗_W k, Γ), where D^×⊗_W k = Spec k((u)). So a 𝒢-torsor on D^× that is trivial on Spec 𝔖[1/E(u)] (hence on Spec k((u))) comes from a 𝒢°-torsor, which is trivial when (3.2.3) holds.
items.note: Numbered displays used to pass from 𝒢 to 𝒢° (the same device reappears in Lemma 3.3.5). Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Integrality test on a normal R_G via O_K-points (cited, de Jong [19, Prop. 7.3.6])
items.statement: Let R_G be normal (and flat over O_E). If s ∈ R_G[1/p] satisfies ξ(s) ∈ O_K for every finite K/E and every ξ: R_G → O_K, then s ∈ R_G.
items.note: Black box, stated as the paper uses it. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Flatness of T over Ŵ(R_G) (cited, Raynaud–Gruson [65, Thm. 4.1.2])
items.statement: (As used) The Ŵ(R_G)-scheme T = Isom_{(s_{α,0})}(M̃_1⊗Ŵ(R_G), M⊗Ŵ(R_G)) is flat over Ŵ(R_G) because ξ*(T) is a trivial 𝒢-torsor over Ŵ(O_K) for every ξ and ∩_ξ ker(Ŵ(ξ)) = 0. Since T also has a nonempty fibre over the closed point, it is a 𝒢-torsor, trivial because k is algebraically closed.
items.note: I did not check the exact statement of [65, 4.1.2]. Ŵ(R_G) is not noetherian. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Deformations of displays over O_K[ε] (cited, Zink [73, Thms. 3, 4])
items.statement: (3.2.16) For any deformation M_{O_K[ε]} of the Dieudonné display M_{O_K} to O_K[ε], there is a Frobenius-equivariant identification M_{O_K[ε]} ≅ M_{O_K}⊗_{Ŵ(O_K)}Ŵ(O_K[ε]) of the underlying Ŵ(O_K[ε])-modules. Isomorphism classes of deformations correspond bijectively to lifts of M̄_{O_K,1} ⊂ M̄_{O_K} to a direct summand M̄_{O_K[ε],1} ⊂ M̄_{O_K[ε]}.
items.note: Black box. The proof of Lemma 3.2.14 combines it with Lemma 3.1.17 to identify M_{O_K[ε]}⊗Q_p with D⊗_W Ŵ(O_K[ε])[1/p], compatibly with Frobenius. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Strictness for weakly admissible tensor constructions (used without citation)
items.statement: End_{K_0}(D_{K_0}) and D^⊗, with their induced structures, are weakly admissible filtered φ-modules, and morphisms of weakly admissible filtered φ-modules are strict. Hence, since the map End(D_{K_0}) → (D^⊗)_α, g ↦ g(s_{α,0}), is a morphism of such modules: if g ∈ End_K(D_K) and g(s_{α,0}) ∈ Fil^0 D_K^⊗ for all α, then g ∈ Lie G + Lie P_ξ.
items.note: Needs the theorem that tensor products of weakly admissible modules are weakly admissible (Faltings, Totaro), which the paper does not cite. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Tensor-adapted tangent modules Def_G(ξ;O_K[ε]) and Def_G(M_{O_K};O_K[ε])
items.statement: Def_G(ξ;O_K[ε]) is the set of lifts of ξ to a map R_G → O_K[ε]. Def_G(M_{O_K};O_K[ε]) is the set of isomorphism classes of deformations of M_{O_K} to a Dieudonné display over O_K[ε] satisfying Lemma 3.2.14(3). Both are free O_K-modules of rank dim R_G[1/p] = dim Lie G/(Lie P_ξ ∩ Lie G). The natural map Def_G(ξ;O_K[ε]) → Def_G(M_{O_K};O_K[ε]) is injective, by the versality of 𝒢_{R_E} and Lemma 3.1.15.
items.note: Introduced in the proof and essential for (3) ⇒ (2). Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: R_G[1/p] is regular
items.statement: R_G[1/p] is regular, and its dimension at each O_K-point ξ is dim Lie G/(Lie G ∩ Lie P_ξ). Reason: the generic fibre of M^loc_G is the smooth orbit G·y ≅ G/(G∩P_y), and R_G is the completion of the excellent scheme M^loc_G at a closed point.
items.locator: used in the proofs of Lemma 3.2.14 (printed p. 175) and Proposition 3.2.17 (printed p. 177: 'Since R_G[1/p] is regular')
items.note: Unnumbered fact used without proof; it is standard. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Display over O_K[[T]] interpolating y and 𝒢_{O_K}; the ideals I_n, J_G, J_G^n
items.statement: (Proof of Proposition 3.2.17, after reducing to y = y' and K' = K.) Let (M_{O_K}, M_{O_K,1}, Φ_1, Φ) be the display of y, with Ψ: M̃_{O_K,1} ≅ M_{O_K} (Lemma 3.1.5; it takes s_{α,0} to s_{α,0}). Let Ψ': M̃_{O_K,1} ≅ M_{O_K} give 𝒢_{O_K}; it takes s_{α,0} to s_{α,0} and reduces to Ψ_0. Put S = O_K[[T]]. The map S → O_K×_k O_K, T ↦ (0,π), is surjective, and so is Ŵ(S) → Ŵ(O_K)×_W Ŵ(O_K). There is Ψ_S: M̃_{S,1} ≅ M_S taking s_{α,0} to s_{α,0} and specializing to (Ψ,Ψ'); M_S denotes the associated display. By versality, (y,ξ): R_E → O_K×_k O_K lifts to ξ̃: R_E → S inducing M_S. Let S_n = S/T^n, I_n = ker(R_E → S_n), J_G = ker(R_E → R_G), 𝔫 = ker(y: R_G → O_K) and J^n_G = ker(R_E → (R_G/𝔫^n)[1/p]). By Lemma 3.2.13, the canonical map of Lemma 3.1.17 for the display over R_E/(I_n∩J^n_G) sends s_{α,0} to s_{α,0}. So by Lemma 3.2.14, maps R_E → O_K[ε] through R_E/(I_n∩J^n_G) factor through R_G.
items.note: Key construction of the proof. 'By Corollary 3.2.11' for Ψ_S is loose: triviality comes from base change of T_y. Lifting (Ψ,Ψ') also uses smoothness of 𝒢 and a henselian property of Ŵ(S) → Ŵ(O_K×_k O_K). Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Étale tensors, their Kisin-module images, ρ and κ_G
items.statement: (3.3.3) Let L ∈ Rep^{criso}_{Γ_K} and let s_{α,ét} ∈ L^⊗ be Γ_K-invariant tensors defining a subgroup 𝒢 ⊂ GL(L), smooth over Z_p with reductive generic fibre G. Applying 𝔐 gives tensors s̃_α ∈ 𝔐(L)^⊗. The Γ_K-action gives ρ: Γ_K → 𝒢(Z_p) ⊂ G(Q_p) (printed '𝒢(Q_p)'). κ_G: G(K_0) → π_1(G)_I, with I = Gal(K̄/K_0), is the Kottwitz homomorphism.
items.locator: 3.3.3 and the paragraph before Proposition 3.3.4, printed pp. 178–179
items.note: The setting for Proposition 3.3.4 through Corollary 3.3.6. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Tannakian construction of torsors on a Dedekind scheme (cited, Broshi [9, Lemma 3.1, Thms. 4.3, 4.5])
items.statement: (As used) Write O_{𝒢°} = lim→ L_i with L_i ⊂ O_{𝒢°} 𝒢°-stable of finite Z_p-rank ([9, Lemma 3.1]). An exact faithful tensor functor from Z_p-free representations of 𝒢° to vector bundles on the Dedekind scheme D^× (here L ↦ 𝔐(L)|_{D^×}, via ρ) makes 𝔐(O_{𝒢°})|_{D^×} = lim→ 𝔐(L_i) a sheaf of algebras, and 𝒫° = Spec 𝔐(O_{𝒢°})|_{D^×} is a 𝒢°-torsor ([9, Thm. 4.3]). The same holds for 𝒢. The functor is recovered as 𝔐(L) ≅ 𝒫×^𝒢 L ([9, Thm. 4.5]).
items.note: Black box. It needs ρ to factor through 𝒢°(Z_p) so that the L_i lie in Rep^{criso}. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Parahoric points equal the Kottwitz kernel in the stabilizer (cited, Haines–Rapoport [38, Prop. 3])
items.statement: For 𝒢 = 𝒢_x the Bruhat–Tits stabilizer of x ∈ B(G,Q_p) and 𝒢° the parahoric, 𝒢°(Z_p) = 𝒢(Z_p) ∩ ker κ_G.
items.note: Black box. [38] states it over the completed maximal unramified extension; the Z_p-points version follows. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Crystalline tensors s_{α,0} of a deformation; standing tame assumptions
items.statement: (3.3.7) Keep 3.3.3 with L = T_p𝒢^∨ for a p-divisible group 𝒢 over O_K with special fibre 𝒢_0. The s_{α,0} ∈ Fil^0 D_cris(T_p𝒢^∨⊗Q_p)^⊗ are the φ-invariant tensors corresponding to s_{α,ét} under the p-adic comparison isomorphism. From here on, 𝒢 = 𝒢_x for some x ∈ B(G,Q_p), and G splits over a tamely ramified extension and has no factors of type E_8.
items.note: Defines the s_{α,0} of §3.3 and the hypotheses of Proposition 3.3.8 through Proposition 3.3.13. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: The group 𝒢_W ⊂ GL(D) and G_{K_0}
items.statement: (3.3.9) Let D = D(𝒢_0)(W). By Proposition 3.3.8, the subgroup 𝒢_W ⊂ GL(D) defined by the s_{α,0} is identified with 𝒢⊗_{Z_p}W; up to 𝒢_W-conjugacy the identification does not depend on the choice of D ≅ W⊗_{Z_p}T_p𝒢^∨. Set G_{K_0} = 𝒢_W⊗_W K_0.
items.note: Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Deformation setup for 𝒢_0 with the tensors s_{α,0}; assumption (3.3.12)
items.statement: (3.3.11) Apply 3.1.8 and §3.2 to 𝒢_0 with the s_{α,0}. P_0 ⊂ GL(D⊗_W k) is the parabolic of the filtration on D⊗_W k and P ⊂ GL(D) a lift. The filtration of Corollary 3.3.10 is a point y ∈ GL(D)/P reducing to P_0. M̂^loc = M̂^loc_y = Spf R and M̂^loc_G = M̂^loc_{G,y} = Spf R_G are defined over O_E, from the orbit G·y, with E/K_0 the reflex field of μ_y. By Proposition 3.3.8, (D,(s_{α,0})) satisfies (3.2.2). Since 𝒢_W = 𝒢⊗_{Z_p}W, H^1(D^×,𝒢°_W) = {1} (Proposition 1.4.3), i.e. (3.2.3). (3.3.12): assume R_G is normal and G contains the scalars. One then fixes Ψ: M̃_{R_E,1} ≅ M_{R_E} (printed 'M̃_1 ≅ M') lifting Ψ_0, constant modulo a_{R_E}, whose base change Ψ_{R_G} respects the s_{α,0}. By E2, this choice exists only under the KPZ26 'very good' condition.
items.note: The standing hypotheses of Proposition 3.3.13; §4.2 (Prop. 4.2.2) invokes this construction. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Shimura datum notation: μ_h, w_h, reflex field, Sh_K, Sh(G,X), Sh_{K_p}(G,X)
items.statement: (G,X) is a Shimura datum ([20] §2.1): G is a connected reductive Q-group and X a G(R)-conjugacy class of h: S = Res_{C/R}G_m → G_R. For a C-algebra R, μ_h is the cocharacter R^× → (R × c^*(R))^× = (R ⊗_R C)^× = S(R) →h G_C(R), and w_h := μ_h^{-1}μ_h^{c−1}. For K = K_pK^p ⊂ G(A_f) compact open (K_p ⊂ G(Q_p), K^p ⊂ G(A_f^p)) with K^p sufficiently small, Sh_K(G,X)_C = G(Q)\X × G(A_f)/K is an algebraic variety with a model Sh_K(G,X) over E = E(G,X), the field of definition of the conjugacy class of μ_h. Sh(G,X) = lim_K Sh_K(G,X) and Sh_{K_p}(G,X) = lim_{K^p} Sh_{K_pK^p}(G,X); these limits exist because the transition maps are finite.
items.note: Standing assumption: K^p is sufficiently small. w_h is used in the proof of 4.2.2 to show that G contains the scalars. The canonical model itself may be covered by foundational P13. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Symplectic similitude group and Siegel double space
items.statement: For a Q-vector space V with a perfect alternating pairing ψ, GSp = GSp(V,ψ) is the group of symplectic similitudes. S± is the set of h: S → GSp_R such that (1) the C^×-action on V_R is a Hodge structure of type (−1,0),(0,−1), V_C ≅ V^{−1,0} ⊕ V^{0,−1}, and (2) (x,y) ↦ ψ(x,h(i)y) is (positive or negative) definite on V_R.
items.note: Possibly covered by foundational P12. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Closed embedding of the Hodge-type Shimura variety into a Siegel variety (cited)
items.statement: ([43] Lemma 2.1.2) With K_p = 𝒢(Z_p) and K'_p = 𝒢𝒮𝒫(Z_p), for any compact open K^p ⊂ G(A_f^p) there is a compact open K'^p ⊂ GSp(A_f^p) such that ι induces an embedding Sh_K(G,X) ↪ Sh_{K'}(GSp,S±) over E.
items.note: Black box. Used to define 𝒮^−_K(G,X). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Integral tensors cutting out G_{Z_(p)} (cited)
items.statement: ([43] Lemma 1.3.2) There is a finite collection of tensors (s_α) ⊂ V^⊗_{Z_(p)} whose stabilizer in GL(V_{Z_(p)}) is G_{Z_(p)}, the Zariski closure of G in GL(V_{Z_(p)}).
items.note: Black box. S02 uses it. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: The Hodge filtration at a lift is G-split (cited)
items.statement: ([43] Lemma 1.4.5) For x ∈ Sh_K(G,X)(K), K/E^ur finite, with specialization x̄, the filtration on D_K := D_x̄ ⊗ K corresponding to 𝒢_x is induced by a G_{K_0} ⊗ K-valued cocharacter, and this cocharacter lies in the G-conjugacy class of μ_h^{-1}.
items.note: Black box. It gives y(x) and μ_y. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Formal local models M̂^loc_y = Spf R and M̂^loc_{G,y} = Spf R_G attached to a specializing point
items.statement: Let K/E^ur be finite and x ∈ Sh_K(G,X)(K) with specialization x̄ ∈ 𝒮^−_K(G,X)(k). Let 𝒢_x be its p-divisible group, D_x̄ = D(𝒢_x̄)(W), s_{α,0} ∈ D_x̄^⊗ ⊗ Q_p the φ-invariant tensors corresponding to s_{α,ét,x}, and G_{K_0} ⊂ GL(D_x̄ ⊗ Q_p) the group they define. With the notation of 3.3.11 applied to 𝒢 = 𝒢_x, we have a parabolic P ⊂ GL(D_x̄) and y = y(x) ∈ (GL(D_x̄)/P)(K) specializing to P_0 = P ⊗_W k and induced by a G-valued μ_y conjugate to μ_h^{-1}. M̂^loc_y = Spf R is the completion of GL(D_x̄)/P at the specialization of y. M̂^loc_{G,y} = Spf R_G is the completion there of the orbit closure M^loc_G := closure of G_{K_0}·y(x) ⊂ GL(D_x̄)/P.
items.note: Used in Proposition 4.2.2 and the proof of Theorem 4.2.7. The paper writes 'defined over O_E', where E is §3's reflex field of μ_y over K_0, that is E^ur in §4's notation. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: de Rham and étale Hodge cycles correspond under the p-adic comparison (cited)
items.statement: ([5]; Blasius, Wintenberger) For x ∈ Sh_K(G,X)(K), K a finite extension of E (or of E^ur), the p-adic comparison isomorphism between H^1_ét(𝒜_{x,K̄},Q_p) and H^1_dR(𝒜_x) takes s_{α,ét,x} to s_{α,dR,x}.
items.locator: Proofs of Proposition 4.2.2 (printed p. 185) and Proposition 4.2.6 (p. 186), and footnote 6
items.note: Black box. Bibliography entry [5] is Blasius alone. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Crystalline–de Rham comparison and uniqueness of parallel sections over a residue disc (cited)
items.statement: ([4] §2.9) For x' ∈ Û_x̄(K'), H^1_cris(𝒜_x̄/W) ⊗_W K' ≅ H^1_dR(𝒜_{x'}), and this takes s_{α,0} to s̃_{α,0}|_{x'}. ([42] 3.1, with [19] §7 for the analytic space 𝒰 of Spf R) Since D_R = D ⊗_W R underlies an F-isocrystal on R, the s_{α,0} extend uniquely to parallel sections s̃_{α,0} ∈ D_R^⊗|_𝒰. A parallel section vanishing at one point vanishes on the irreducible component containing it.
items.note: Black boxes. They are used to show that s_{α,ét,x'} corresponds to s_{α,0} on the whole component of x. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Base-changed and completed local models M^loc_{G,X,z}, M̂^loc_{G,X,z}
items.statement: For an extension of perfect fields k'/k_E and z ∈ M^loc_{G,X}(k'), M^loc_{G,X,z} := M^loc_{G,X} ⊗_{W(k_E)} W(k'), and M̂^loc_{G,X,z} is its completion at the image of z.
items.note: Used in Corollary 4.2.4. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: de Rham bundle, its integral extension, and the generic torsor of tensor frames
items.statement: 𝒱 = R^1h_*Ω^• over Sh_K(G,X), with the absolute Hodge cycles s_{α,dR} ∈ 𝒱^⊗ defined over E, extends to the bundle 𝒱̲ over 𝒮_K(G,X): the first de Rham cohomology of the pulled-back universal abelian scheme. Sh̃_K(G,X) → Sh_K(G,X) is the G-torsor of trivializations f: V^∨ ≅ 𝒱 with f^⊗(s_α) = s_{α,dR}.
items.note: The paper asserts the torsor property over Sh_K; it follows from the theory of absolute Hodge cycles ([43] §2.2). Proposition 4.2.6 extends it integrally. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Local frame diagram (4.2.9)
items.statement: By Proposition 3.3.4 and Proposition 3.3.8 (printed 'Lemma 3.3.8'), s_{α,0,x̄} ∈ D_x̄^⊗. Let M̃^loc_G → M^loc_G be the scheme of isomorphisms f: D_x̄ ≅ V^∨_{Z_p} ⊗_{Z_p} W with f^⊗(s_{α,0,x̄}) = s_α. Then M̃^loc_G = 𝒫 × M^loc_G with 𝒫 a trivial 𝒢_W-torsor, so π^loc: M̃^loc_G → M^loc_G is a 𝒢-torsor. q^loc: M̃^loc_G → M^loc_{G,X} ⊗ O_{E^ur} sends (f,ℱ) to f(ℱ) (printed f^{-1}(ℱ)). q^loc is isomorphic to the action morphism 𝒢 × M^loc_{G,X} → M^loc_{G,X}, so it is smooth of relative dimension dim G.
items.note: The proof of 4.2.7 uses the local diagram through (4.2.11): the completion of (4.2.10) at x̄ is identified with the pullback of (4.2.9). See E4 and the new misprint on f^{-1}(ℱ). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Parahorics in hyperspecial subgroups are connected stabilizers (Remark 4.2.14 b)
