items.statement: Let G be unramified over Q_p (quasi-split and split over an unramified extension). If x ∈ B(G,Q_p) and 𝒢_x°(Z_p) is contained in a hyperspecial subgroup, then there is x' ∈ B(G,Q_p) with 𝒢_x° = 𝒢_{x'}: one can take x' to be a generic point of the smallest facet containing x ([35], Corrigendum, Lemma 7.0.2). Hence Theorem 4.2.7 and its corollaries apply to all such parahoric subgroups.
items.note: Used later in Theorem 4.6.23(5) and cited near Corollary 4.6.26. It is the form in which the connectedness hypothesis of 4.2.12–4.2.13 is actually met. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: A conjugacy class of cocharacters of a quasi-split group has a representative in a maximal torus defined over the field of definition (implicitly cited)
items.statement: If G_{E_0} is quasi-split and T is the centralizer of a maximal split torus, then the class [μ_h^{-1}], which is defined over E, contains a cocharacter μ ∈ X_*(T) that is defined over E (Kottwitz, [45] Lemma 1.1.3).
items.note: Used without citation. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Kottwitz kernel and parahorics: K° = K ∩ ker κ_G and T°(O) ⊂ 𝒢°_x(O) (cited)
items.statement: ([38] Prop. 3) 𝒢°(Z_p) = 𝒢(Z_p) ∩ ker κ_G. For a torus T over a p-adic field F, the connected Néron model satisfies T°(O_F) = ker(κ_T: T(F) → (X_*(T)_I)^σ). If x lies in the apartment of T, then T°(O_F) ⊂ 𝒢_x°(O_F).
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 4.3.2 and Lemma 4.3.5, printed pp. 189–190
items.note: Black box. It may overlap A's G01 and foundational P02. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Deligne's congruence-subgroup facts (cited)
items.statement: ([20] Cor. 2.0.5, 2.0.13) With ρ: G̃ → G, for K^p sufficiently small, K^p ∩ G(Q) ⊂ (ρG̃(A_f^p) ∩ G(Q))·U for any finite-index subgroup U of the p-units of Z_G(Q). ([20] Prop. 2.0.4(ii)) Under (4.3.4), ρG̃(A_f^p) ∩ G(Q) = ρG̃(A_f) ∩ G(Q), with the intersections taken in G(A_f^p) and G(A_f) respectively.
items.note: Black box. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Connected components of Shimura varieties and the Galois action on them (cited)
items.statement: ([20] 2.1.3.1) The geometric connected components of Sh_K(G,X) form a torsor under the abelian group G(A_f)/G(Q)_+K. ([20] Thm. 2.6.3) Gal(Q̄/E) acts on π_0(Sh_{K_p}(G,X)_{Q̄}) through the reciprocity map built from the conjugacy class of μ_h^{-1} and the norm.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.3.7 and Corollary 4.3.9, printed pp. 190–191
items.note: Black box. Combined with Lemma 4.3.2, it gives the splitting over an unramified extension and Corollary 4.3.9. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: G(Q)_+, G(Q)_+^−, H_+, G^ad(Q)^+, Z(Q)^−, Z(Z_(p))^−
items.statement: G(Q)_+ is the preimage of G^ad(R)^+ in G(Q), and G(Q)_+^− its closure in G(A_f). More generally, for H ⊂ G(R), H_+ is the preimage in H of G^ad(R)^+, the identity component of G^ad(R). G^ad(Q)^+ = G^ad(Q) ∩ G^ad(R)^+. Z(Q)^− is the closure of Z_G(Q) in G(A_f), and Z(Z_(p))^− the closure of Z(Z_(p)) in G(A_f^p).
items.note: Used in 4.3.7, 4.5.6 and §4.6. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: The torsor π° over the parahoric-level model (and the authors' conjecture)
items.statement: Pulling back the 𝒢-torsor π of Theorem 4.2.7 along 𝒮_{K°}(G,X) → 𝒮_K(G,X) gives a 𝒢-torsor π°: 𝒮̃_{K°}(G,X) → 𝒮_{K°}(G,X). The authors conjecture, without proof, that it reduces to a 𝒢°-torsor.
items.note: The conjecture is stated as open, not as a result. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Abelian schemes up to A-isogeny and Aut_A
items.statement: For A ⊂ Q and a scheme S, the A-isogeny category of abelian schemes over S is obtained by applying ⊗_Z A to the Hom groups. Its objects are abelian schemes up to A-isogeny, and 𝒜(T) := Hom_S(T,𝒜) ⊗_Z A. Aut_A(𝒜) is the A-group with Aut_A(𝒜)(R) = ((End_S 𝒜) ⊗_Z R)^× for A-algebras R.
items.note: S18 and S19 depend on it. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Moret-Bailly: torsors acquire points over finite integral extensions (cited)
items.statement: ([55] Thm. 1.6, as used) If A ⊂ Q and 𝒫 is a torsor under a flat affine group scheme of finite type over A, there is a finite, integral, torsion-free A-algebra A' with 𝒫(A') ≠ ∅. In particular, 𝒫(O_{F,(p)}) ≠ ∅ for a suitable Galois number field F.
items.note: Black box. Planned: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1 plans Moret-Bailly's theorem.

items.name: Homomorphisms of abelian schemes extend over normal bases (cited)
items.statement: ([23] I, 2.7) If S is normal and noetherian and U ⊂ S is dense open, every homomorphism of abelian schemes over U extends uniquely to S.
items.note: Black box. It reduces Lemma 4.5.2 to T = Sh_K(G,X). Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: The centre acts on the universal abelian variety up to isogeny (cited)
items.statement: ([43] Lemmas 3.2.2, 3.4.1) There is a natural embedding Z ⊗_{Z_(p)} Q ↪ Aut_Q(𝒜_x) for x ∈ Sh_K(G,X)(T). At y ∈ Sh_K(G,X)(C) it is the action of Z ⊂ G on H_1(𝒜_y(C),Q) ≅ V obtained from a lift ỹ ∈ X × G(A_f).
items.note: Black box. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Prime-to-p Tate modules, level-structure sheaves and the triple description of Siegel points
items.statement: For an abelian scheme ℬ up to Z_(p)-isogeny over a Z_(p)-scheme T, V̂^p(ℬ) = lim_{p∤n} ℬ[n] and V̂^p(ℬ)_{Z_(p)} = V̂^p(ℬ) ⊗ Z_(p) = V̂^p(ℬ) ⊗ Q. If dim ℬ = dim V/2 and ℬ has a weak Z_(p)-polarization λ, Isom(V_{A_f^p}, V̂^p(ℬ)_Q) is the pro-étale sheaf of isomorphisms respecting the pairings from ψ and λ up to A_f^{p,×}, and Isom/K'^p is étale. A point x ∈ 𝒮_{K'}(GSp,S±)(T) corresponds to a triple (𝒜_x, λ_x, ε_x^p). For x ∈ 𝒮_K(G,X)(T), ε_x^p lifts to Γ(T, Isom/K^p) ([43] (3.2.4)). For x ∈ 𝒮_{K_p}(G,X)(T), ε_x^p ∈ lim_{K^p} Γ(T, Isom/K^p).
items.note: Needed to define the twisted triple of Lemma 4.5.7. The triple description leaves out the p-primary degree condition on λ; see notes. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: The central torsor of an adjoint element and its trivializing isogeny ι_γ̃
items.statement: G^ad_{Z_(p)} := G_{Z_(p)}/Z, with Z the closure of the centre. For γ ∈ G^ad_{Z_(p)}(Z_(p)), 𝒫 is the fibre of G_{Z_(p)} → G^ad_{Z_(p)} over γ, which is a Z-torsor. Choose F/Q Galois and γ̃ ∈ 𝒫(O_{F,(p)}) ([55]). Lemma 4.5.2 and (4.4.4) specialized at γ̃ give a Z_(p)-isogeny ι_γ̃: 𝒜_x^𝒫 ⊗_{Z_(p)} O_{F,(p)} ≅ 𝒜_x ⊗_{Z_(p)} O_{F,(p)}.
items.note: γ is misprinted as 'γ ∈ G_{Z_(p)}(Z_(p))'. S22, S25 and S26 use this construction. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Kisin's twisting lemmas used for the adjoint action (cited)
items.statement: ([43] Lemma 3.1.5, argument) Twisting a c-polarization gives a unique weak polarization; see Lemma 4.4.8. ([43] Lemma 3.2.6, argument) On generic fibres, (𝒜_x,λ_x,ε_x^p) ↦ (𝒜_x^𝒫, λ_x^𝒫, ε_x^{p,𝒫}) factors through Sh_{K_p}(G,X) and induces conjugation by γ. ([43] Lemma 3.4.3) σ(ι_γ̃) = c_γ̃(σ)^{-1}ι_γ̃ for σ ∈ Gal(F/Q), where c_γ̃(σ) = σ(γ̃)γ̃^{-1} ∈ Z(O_{F,(p)}).
items.locator: Lemma 4.4.8 (p. 193), proof of Lemma 4.5.7 (p. 196), proof of Lemma 4.5.9 (p. 197)
items.note: Black boxes. The proof of Lemma 4.5.4 cites '[43] Lemma 3.4', an incomplete number. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: The pulled-back torsor 𝒮̃_{K_p} and the adjoint torsor 𝒮̃^ad_{K_p}
items.statement: 𝒮̃_{K_p} = 𝒮̃_{K_p}(G,X) is the pullback of the G_{Z_(p)}-torsor 𝒮̃_K(G,X)_{O_E} of Theorem 4.2.7 to 𝒮_{K_p}(G,X), and 𝒮̃^ad_{K_p} := 𝒮̃_{K_p}/Z is the induced G^ad_{Z_(p)}-torsor. The map q of (4.2.8) factors through 𝒮̃^ad_{K_p} because Z acts trivially on M^loc_{G,X}: Z commutes with μ, so it fixes y and hence the flat closure of G·y.
items.note: S26 depends on it. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Z_(p)-models G_{Z_(p)}, G°, G^ad_{Z_(p)}, G^der_{Z_(p)}, G^{ad°}, G^{der°}
items.statement: G_{Z_(p)} is the Z_(p)-model of G obtained by the descent of §4.6.1 from the Bruhat–Tits stabilizer 𝒢_x of x ∈ B(G,Q_p); G^ad_{Z_(p)} := G_{Z_(p)}/Z_{Z_(p)} with Z_{Z_(p)} the closure of the centre Z; G^der_{Z_(p)} := the closure of G^der in G_{Z_(p)}; G° = G°_{Z_(p)} is the identity component (the descent of the parahoric 𝒢_x°); G^{ad°} = G^{ad°}_{Z_(p)} and G^{der°} = G^{der°}_{Z_(p)} are the descents of the parahoric group schemes of G^ad and G^der attached to the image x^ad of x in B(G^ad,Q_p) = B(G^der,Q_p). In general G^{ad°}_{Z_(p)} is not the identity component of G^ad_{Z_(p)} (cf. Lemma 4.6.2(2)).
items.note: Used in Lemmas 4.6.2, 4.6.4, the definitions of §4.6.3 and throughout §4.6. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Extension of the 𝒜(G_{Z_(p)})-action to 𝒮_{K_p} and 𝒮_{K_p°}
items.statement: Assume (from here on) that Z = Z_G is connected or Z_{G^der} has rank prime to p. Then, by Lemma 4.6.2(2) and Lemma 4.5.7, the action of 𝒜(G_{Z_(p)}) on Sh_{K_p}(G,X) extends to 𝒮_{K_p}(G,X); with 𝒮_{K_p°}(G,X) the normalization of 𝒮_{K_p}(G,X) in Sh_{K_p°}(G,X), the action of 𝒜(G_{Z_(p)}) on Sh_{K_p°}(G,X) extends to 𝒮_{K_p°}(G,X).
items.note: Invoked as 'As observed in 4.6.3' in the proof of Corollary 4.6.15; S24 defines the groups but not this extension. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Setting of §4.6.8: the second datum (G_2,X_2) and its groups
items.statement: G_2 is a reductive group over Q with a central isogeny α: G^der → G_2^der; x_2 ∈ B(G_2,Q_p) with x_2^ad = x^ad; 𝒢_2 (resp. 𝒢_2°) the stabilizer (resp. parahoric) model of x_2, with Z_(p)-models G_{2,Z_(p)}, G°_{2,Z_(p)}, and K°_{2,p} = 𝒢_2°(Z_p). (G_2,X_2) is a Shimura datum with α inducing (G^ad,X^ad) ≅ (G_2^ad,X_2^ad); after conjugating X_2 by G_2^ad(Q) the image of X_2 in X_2^ad contains X^+. E_2 is the reflex field of (G_2,X_2), E' = E·E_2, and ℰ_{E'}(G°), ℰ̃_{E'}(G°) are the pullbacks of ℰ(G°), ℰ̃(G°) along Gal(E'^p/E') → Gal(E^p/E), Gal(Ē/E') → Gal(Ē/E). One sets 𝒜(G_{2,Z_(p)}) = G_2(A_f^p)/Z_{G_2}(Z_(p))^- *_{G_2°(Z_(p))_+/Z_{G_2}(Z_(p))} G^{ad°}(Z_(p))^+ (the same G^{ad°}(Z_(p))^+ as for G), similarly Ã(G_{2,Z_(p)})°. The geometrically connected components of Sh_{K°_{2,p}}(G_2,X_2) are defined over E_2^p (as in Corollary 4.3.9); ℰ(G°_{2,Z_(p)}) ⊂ 𝒜(G_{2,Z_(p)}) × Gal(E_2^p/E_2) is the stabilizer of Sh_{K°_{2,p}}(G_2,X_2)^+, an extension of Gal(E_2^p/E_2) by 𝒜(G_{2,Z_(p)})°, and ℰ̃(G°_{2,Z_(p)}) is an extension of Gal(Ē/E_2) by Ã(G_{2,Z_(p)})°.
items.note: Only partly absorbed into S32; the definitions of 𝒜(G_{2,Z_(p)}) and ℰ(G°_{2,Z_(p)}) are used in 4.6.9–4.6.18. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: The inclusion of §4.6.12 and the set J
items.statement: By Lemma 4.6.10 there is an inclusion 𝒜(G_{Z_(p)})°\𝒜(G_{2,Z_(p)}) = Ã(G_{Z_(p)})°\Ã(G_{2,Z_(p)})/K°_{2,p} ↪ 𝒜(G)°\𝒜(G_2)/K°_{2,p}. J ⊂ G_2(Q_p) is a set mapping bijectively to a set of coset representatives for the image of 𝒜(G_{2,Z_(p)}) in 𝒜(G)°\𝒜(G_2)/K°_{2,p} (i.e. for the orbits of that image; since 𝒜(G)° is normal in 𝒜(G_2) with abelian quotient, left and right cosets agree).
items.note: S34 refers to 'the representatives j of 4.6.12' but J has no item. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Deligne's reciprocity law for π_0 (cited [20] Thm. 2.6.3)
items.statement: The action of Gal(Ē/E) on the geometrically connected components of Sh(G,X) is given by composing the Artin reciprocity isomorphism with the map (4.6.7): A_E^×/E^×(E ⊗_Q R)^{×,+} = A_E^{f×}/E^{×,+} → G(A_E^f)/G(E)^-_+ → G(A_f)/G(Q)^-_+, the first map induced by μ_h^{-1} and the second by N_{E/Q}, where E^{×,+} = E^× ∩ (E ⊗ R)^{×,+} and G(E)^-_+ = (R_{E/Q}G)(Q)^-_+.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 4.6.6, printed p. 200 (also §4.6.5, Cor. 4.3.9)
items.note: Black box from Deligne, Variétés de Shimura (Corvallis). Combined with Lemma 4.3.2 it gives the surjectivity statements of Lemma 4.6.6(1). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Deligne's description of Sh(G_2,X_2) from Sh(G,X)^+ (cited [20] 2.5.6, 2.7.11, 2.7.13)
items.statement: In the setting of §4.6.8, there is a morphism of extensions ℰ_{E'}(G) → ℰ(G_2) (ℰ(G) ⊂ 𝒜(G) × Gal(Ē/E) the stabilizer of Sh(G,X)^+, an extension of Gal(Ē/E) by 𝒜(G)°), hence 𝒜(G_2) *_{𝒜(G)°} ℰ_{E'}(G) ≅ 𝒜(G_2) × Gal(Ē/E'); letting ℰ_{E'}(G) act on the right on Sh(G,X)^+ × 𝒜(G_2) by (s,a)·e = (se, ē^{-1}aē) and 𝒜(G_2) by right multiplication, one gets an isomorphism of Ē-schemes with G_2(A_f) × Gal(Ē/E')-action Sh(G_2,X_2) ≅ [Sh(G,X)^+ × 𝒜(G_2)]/𝒜(G)°.
items.note: The printed proof writes the amalgam as ≅ G_2(A_f) × Gal(Ē/E') (misprint, see sourceIssues). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: The group H^♯ and the abelian-type criterion (§4.6.21, cited [20], [43] 3.4.13)
items.statement: For a Shimura datum (H,Y) such that (H^ad,Y^ad) is of abelian type (in particular H^ad classical), there is a central isogeny H̃ → H^♯ (depending also on Y if H has a factor of type D) such that (H,Y) is of abelian type if and only if H^der is a quotient of H^♯. H^♯ = H^sc except for factors of type D^H, where it is the image of H^sc in the standard orthogonal representation (for type D the non-compact places must all be D^R or all D^H).
items.note: Printed for all classical H^ad; see E7. Used in Lemma 4.6.22 only for (G_2,X_2) of abelian type. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Deligne's Hodge-type lifting (cited [20] 2.3.10, 2.3.2)
items.statement: As used in the proof of Lemma 4.6.22: (a) for (G_2,X_2) of abelian type with G_2^ad = ∏_i Res_{F_i/Q}G'_i there is a Hodge-type (G,X) with G^der = ∏_i Res_{F_i/Q}G_i'^♯ and a central isogeny G^der → G_2^der inducing (G^ad,X^ad) ≅ (G_2^ad,X_2^ad); for G^ad = Res_{F/Q}G', built from a CM quadratic extension K/F and a set T of embeddings K ↪ C mapping bijectively to the compact places I_c, one can arrange E(G,X) = E^ad·E(K^×,h_T), and Z_G lies in a product of Z_{G^der}, K^× and a torus split over the fixed field of the kernel of the Galois action on the Dynkin diagram of G^ad. (b) ([20] Prop. 2.3.2) If G' acts faithfully on W with a Hodge structure of type {(−1,0),(0,−1)} given by h' and ad h'(i) is a Cartan involution of G'_R/w_{h'}(G_m), then there is an alternating form on W giving a Hodge embedding (G',X') ↪ (GSp(W),S^±_W).
items.note: Black boxes from Deligne 1979. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Étale local structure at finite prime-to-p level (Remark 4.6.25(a))
items.statement: If K_2^p ⊂ G_2(A_f^p) is sufficiently small, the conclusions of Theorem 4.6.23 about étale local structure also hold for the quotient 𝒮_{K_2°}(G_2,X_2) = 𝒮_{K°_{2,p}}(G_2,X_2)/K_2^p.
items.note: Needed for Corollary 4.6.26 and §4.7, which work at finite level with K^p sufficiently small. Printed with (G,X) in place of (G_2,X_2) (misprint). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Special fibres of tame local models (cited [59] Thm. 9.1, Cor. 9.4)
items.statement: As used in Corollary 4.6.26: for G tame over Q_p with p ∤ |π_1(G^der)|, the local model M^loc_{G,μ,x} has reduced special fibre whose irreducible components are normal and Cohen–Macaulay; if x is a special vertex of B(G,Q_p^ur), the special fibre is normal and Cohen–Macaulay.
items.note: Black box from Pappas–Zhu 2013, applied to the auxiliary Hodge-type group; p > 2 gives the π_1 hypothesis. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Compactification with Cartier boundary (cited [52])
items.statement: As used in Proposition 4.6.28 (Hodge type, K_p° very special): there is an open embedding 𝒮_{K°}(G,X) ↪ 𝒮̄_{K°}(G,X) into a proper O_{E,v}-scheme whose complement is a relative Cartier divisor and such that 𝒮̄_{K°}(G,X) has normal special fibre.
items.note: Madapusi Pera, toroidal compactifications (arXiv:1211.1731); properness is implicit in the Stein-factorization step. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Extension property gives a common open (cited [54] §2)
items.statement: Two models of Sh_{K°}(G,X) with the extension property of Theorem 4.6.23(3) contain isomorphic open subschemes containing the generic fibre and all generic points of the special fibre.
items.locator: §4.6.27 and proof of Proposition 4.6.28, printed pp. 210–211
items.note: Argument of Milne 1992, §2. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: The ample automorphic line bundle ω_G
items.statement: For (G,X) with G^ad absolutely simple, h ∈ X^ad, T ⊂ G^ad_C a maximal torus with μ_h ∈ X_*(T), B ⊃ T a Borel with μ_h^{-1} dominant, P ⊃ B the parabolic attached to μ_h^{-1} with unipotent radical N: exactly one simple root lies in Lie(N) and X^*(P) ≅ Z. Each χ ∈ X^*(P) gives a line bundle ω_χ on Sh_K(G,X) defined over the reflex field ([53]); ω_G := ω_{χ_0} for the generator χ_0 with ω_{χ_0} ample.
items.note: Printed 'Borel subgroup of G' and 'K ⊂ G(A_F)'; read G^ad_C and G(A_f). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Irreducible special fibres and extensions of ω_G (very special level)
items.statement: Let (G,X) be as in Corollary 4.6.26 with K_p° very special. Then every irreducible component of 𝒮_{K°}(G,X) has irreducible special fibre; hence any two extensions to 𝒮_{K°}(G,X) of a line bundle on Sh_{K°}(G,X) differ by an automorphism of ω_G which is a scalar on each irreducible component; and for some n > 0, ω_G^{⊗n} extends to an ample line bundle on 𝒮_{K°}(G,X).
items.note: Intermediate results of the proof of 4.6.28 (via [52], Stein factorization and pullback of ω_GSp). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Extension property of the Siegel tower (Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich)
items.statement: Let 𝒮_{K'_p}(GSp,S^±) = lim_{K'^p} 𝒮_{K'_pK'^p}(GSp,S^±) (models of 4.2.1). For every discrete valuation ring R of mixed characteristic (0,p), 𝒮_{K'_p}(GSp,S^±)(R) → 𝒮_{K'_p}(GSp,S^±)(R[1/p]) is a bijection: an R[1/p]-point is an abelian variety with trivialized l-adic Tate modules for all l ≠ p, hence has good reduction.
items.note: Input to S46. Missing: routed to route 9.

routes.reason: Existing valued-local-group owner: add the exact central-kernel, minuscule building/fixer and Lang statements as proof inputs to its models and double-coset scope. Do not rebuild upstream reductive groups, pinning or roots.

Generic Hartogs extension, affine arithmetic descent and module torsor twisting use the existing scheme/descent owner. Import the earlier CESNAVICIUS-22 torsor and patching items before adding statement-specific adapters.

The A-isogeny twist, weak polarization and structured Serre–Tate comparison extend the existing arithmetic Hom/dual/deformation APIs. General torsor descent stays in SF.1; integral Shimura actions are consumers.

LPV owns the actual nearby-cycle functor and its inertia/monodromy filtration. Add semisimple trace on finite-inertia graded pieces with exact-triangle additivity; import the established étale trace and adic-realization suppliers. No second nearby-cycle carrier is created.

routes.title: Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: integral and modular representations
routes.brief: Reuse the KPZ26 candidate beginning after Reductive groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups), especially integral pinned groups Layer9, and Root systems (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/RootSystems) for the root/weight carrier. Add KP18 minuscule integral highest-weight lattices, irreducible reduction (Jantzen II2.15), homothety of stable lattices, rank-one root strings, projective Schur descent through a division algebra and explicit equal-characteristic twisted Weyl data. Prove Proposition1.2.10 with its split irreducible characteristic-zero hypotheses; supply Proposition1.3.3 through the local-group owner rather than own buildings here. Do not assume arbitrary characteristic-p representations semisimple or replace integral divided powers by rational operators. Resolve the Satake primary symplectic cases and integral root-action source gates before closing this branch. Correction: the map (1.2.23)–(1.2.24) of §1.2.22 must use the product over the K-embeddings of K_1 ∩ K^ur when K_1/K is not totally ramified (E13), as §1.3 already does.
routes.reason: Identical candidate owner to KPZ26; these are the original minuscule-lattice inputs it consumes, not a new parallel representation roadmap.

routes.title: Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: arithmetic torsors and purity
routes.brief: Reuse the CESNAVICIUS-22 arithmetic-torsor candidate, beginning with Reductive groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups). Add a distinct punctured-disc branch: for D=Spec W(k)[[u]], k finite or an algebraic closure of Fp, and connected parahoric G with tame reductive generic fiber without E8, prove H1_fppf(D minus closed point,G)=1 (KP18 Proposition1.4.3). This is not a specialization of the candidate’s regular-semilocal quasi-split REDUCTIVE Grothendieck–Serre theorem: the parahoric need not be reductive over D. Import ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.1–4 for fixers/root decompositions, SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0–2/4 for descent, cohomology, Hartogs and patching, and FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory for the Witt coefficient carrier. Split induced-torus H1/H2, flasque cyclic resolution, Serre-II generic triviality over algebraically closed k, completed-boundary triviality, the double-coset factorization and finite-k descent into separate layers. The dimension-two fraction-field argument is only used over algebraically closed k; finite k has prime-to-p cd3. Read the exact Gabber/Kato/Gille/Bayer-Fluckiger–Parimala and Brauer sources and close the no-E8 hypotheses. Export the actual trivialization and tensor-isomorphism extension to display consumers. Corrections: Lemma 1.4.6 holds as proved only for k algebraically closed, the only case used (E17); Step 3 of Proposition 1.4.3 must justify Bruhat–Tits theory over ℰ, whose residue field is imperfect (E21).
routes.reason: Consolidates a new parahoric purity branch with the existing arithmetic-torsor candidate and proposes a broader title. It neither claims the existing GS theorem covers it nor adds a second generic torsor carrier.

routes.title: Geometric Satake over the Fargues–Fontaine curve, Part II: integral local models
routes.brief: Reuse GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII from Kisin–Zhou25/KPZ26, beginning with GeometricSatakeAndFusion. Import GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.1 for equal-characteristic loop geometry, ReductiveGroupsPartII for fixers and integral representations from ReductiveGroupsIntegralRepresentationsPartII. Add the original tame Pappas–Zhu closure, normality under p∤π1derived, geometrically reduced special fiber, normal Cohen–Macaulay Schubert closures and normality after every finite reflex extension; then central/derived-isogeny comparisons, symplectic chain and total-lattice good embeddings. Prove KP18 Theorem2.1.2, Propositions2.2.4/2.2.7/2.3.7 and Corollary2.3.16 with the half-rank flag convention. Add a later nearby-cycle branch importing LPV.0–1 and SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.1/SR.4 plus SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters: prove splitting-field unipotence, very-special triviality, centrality and Bernstein characterization of the local-model trace. Read PZ published10.5/10.9/10.12/10.14/10.16 (v4 §9 numbering) and its Wakimoto/central-sheaf inputs. Keep the raw constant sheaf distinct from IC[d](d/2), and make Haar, Frobenius and shift conventions explicit. Shimura test-function formulas are applications in the integral Shimura owner. Corrections: the proof of Proposition 2.3.7 must account for the degrees m_j of the centralizer division algebras (E29); in §2.3.15 the Grassmannian has rank ½·dim V′ (E31), and Corollary 2.3.16 is deduced through the composite of closed immersions (E33).
routes.reason: Reuses the established integral local-model owner; its later degeneration/central-sheaf branch supplies this paper’s extra arithmetic application without recreating LPV or classical Hecke algebras.

routes.title: Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory, Part II: tensors and displays
routes.brief: Reuse the Kisin–Zhou25/KPZ26 candidate, beginning with FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2/R07.4/R07.6. Import Witt vectors and divided powers from the pinned baseline, local-model rings from GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII, parahoric purity from ReductiveGroupsPartIIGrothendieckSerre, and generic Hartogs/descent from SchemeAndStackFoundations. Develop KP18 §3 with algebraically closed k in §§3.2–3.3, contravariant Dieudonné variance and LINEAR dual Tate modules. Replace Lemma3.1.9’s invalid normal-decomposition connection by KPZ26 §5.1.15–19’s relative-frame τ and residual-to-universal canonical map; require very-good first-order tensor preservation in3.2.12. Prove the corrected versality, tangent lifting, rational Frobenius section in its lattice-induced topology, integral tensor torsors, four tangent criteria and Proposition3.2.17/3.3.13 factorization. Split Breuil–Kisin tensor/exactness/comparison statements, exactness only on D×, Wintenberger Kottwitz image and Broshi tensor torsors. Keep Raynaud–Gruson flatness, pointwise integrality, weak-admissibility strictness and interpolation continuity as explicit proof inputs. Corrections: in Lemma 3.2.9 only φ(E([π])) is a nonzerodivisor (E41); Corollary 3.2.11 must show membership in Zink's Ŵ(R_G), not only W(R_G) (E43); the proof of Proposition 3.2.17 needs the stated completion argument (E46); Proposition 3.3.13 needs the étale tensors of the new deformation to match (E51).
routes.reason: Same tensor/display owner as the two preceding extractions. Original KP18 proofs and their corrections are linked, not counted as independently covered by a carrier stage.

routes.title: Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: integral models and reduction
routes.brief: Reuse the candidate established by KMPS22, Kisin–Zhou25 and KPZ26; its first prerequisite is ShimuraVarieties V1/V6/V8. Import the local-model, display, parahoric, abelian-scheme twisting and LPV/Hecke owners above. Construct the prescribed Siegel parahoric moduli before normalization (PEL M2 good-level smoothness is insufficient), absolute Hodge realizations, corrected adapted deformation rings, integral tensor frames, smooth local-model diagrams and connected-parahoric finite étale normalization. Develop the arithmetic star products, component Galois extensions, central twisting and free quotient descent including potentially infinite kernel and jKp°j^-1 component levels. Prove Lemma4.6.22’s five separate auxiliary-cover outputs only for abelian type, using KPZ26’s corrected cover; prove Theorem4.6.23’s five parts separately and Corollary4.6.26. The DVR extension property is at the full prime-to-p tower. General independence and connected G°-torsor reduction are conjectures in this source, whereas Proposition4.6.28 proves independence only for very special Kp and absolutely simple Gad. Finally prove Corollary4.7.3 and Theorem4.7.11: unramified G, p>2, p∤π1derived, and no D^H or hyperspecial-contained parahoric give Trss(Frob_y,RΨQell)=q^(d/2)z_(μ_h,r)(w). Same-field henselization is required for Frobenius, unlike the geometric inertia comparison. Corrections: Corollaries 4.2.12 (second sentence) and 4.2.13 need 𝒢 = 𝒢°, not only K_p = K_p° (E58); in Lemma 4.6.22(3) the field K must be chosen as F·K_0 with p split in K_0 for every prime of E_2 above p to split (E70).
routes.reason: The established integral Shimura candidate owns global descent and arithmetic applications. Canonical all-case results from the sequel remain a later input, never retroactively attributed to the original paper.

routes.title: Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: parahoric centers
routes.brief: Begin after SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (Smooth representations of local groups), importing SR.1’s convolution/corners, SR.3’s applicable characteristic-zero center carrier, and SR.4’s classical spherical Satake. Import ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.4–5 for matching unramified valued-root/Frobenius data. Construct the Iwahori Bernstein presentation and the isomorphisms from its center to a parahoric center and spherical Hecke algebra by normalized idempotents (Haines2009 Theorem3.1.1 and change-of-parahoric compatibility). Define z_(μ,r) with explicit coefficient field, geometric Frobenius, sqrt(q), cocharacter sign and hyperspecial minuscule value q^(-d/2)1_(KμK). Prove that the equal/mixed-characteristic matching double-coset bijection preserves convolution constants and z. This algebraic owner exports N10–N12 to the local-model central-sheaf proof; it does not depend on the Shimura trace formula it supplies. The existing SmoothRepresentationsPartIIUnitarySpherical candidate classifies unitary/tempered spherical parameters and does not supply these parahoric center maps. sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 3.1.9. — Let a_R = m²_R + pR. There is a canonical commutative diagram [M̃₁ ⊗_{Ŵ(R)} Ŵ(R/a_R) → φ*(M_{R/a_R}); D̃₁ ⊗_W Ŵ(R/a_R) → φ*(D) ⊗_W Ŵ(R/a_R)] where the horizontal maps are induced by the natural inclusions M̃₁ → φ*(M_R) and D̃₁ → φ*(D). Proof. — L ⊕ T be a normal decomposition for (M_{R/a_R}, M_{R/a_R,1}), and let L₀ ⊕ T₀ be the induced normal decomposition for (D, D₁).
sourceIssues.correction: The construction has to be replaced by the one of KPZ26 Lemma 5.1.15, which follows [Ho23] and, in essence, Zink's [Zi99, Theorem 3].
sourceIssues.reason: The map produced by the printed proof depends on the chosen normal decomposition M = L ⊕ T, so it is not canonical and the diagram does not characterise it: as KPZ26 Remark 5.1.17(a) puts it, « the isomorphism which is given by the construction of [KP18, Lem. 3.1.9] is not canonical and hence not “correct” », and the diagram does not determine c because its horizontal maps are not always injective, which can happen even when cW(R) is p-torsion free. Consequently [KP18, Lem. 3.1.12] does not hold with c defined as in the proof of Lemma 3.1.9.

review.reason: Checked on the page image and against KPZ26 v3 (SHA-256 d0834555…, same file as the extraction): §1.3.1 and Rem. 5.1.17(a)–(b) are quoted correctly. Independent check: take a normal decomposition over R and change L to L' spanned by l_i + c_i t with c_i = V([x]), x ∈ m_R \ a_R, keeping T. Then L_0 and T_0 do not change, but φ*(l'_i) = φ*(l_i) + [x]·pφ*(t). The two constructions differ on φ*(l'_i) ⊗ 1 by [x̄]·(pφ*(t_0) ⊗ 1), which is nonzero in the free module D̃_1 ⊗_W Ŵ(R/a_R) (pφ*(t_0) is a basis vector there), while its image p[x̄]φ*(t_0) in φ*(D) ⊗ Ŵ(R/a_R) vanishes because p·W(m_R/a_R) = VF·W(m_R/a_R) = 0. So the map depends on the decomposition, and the diagram cannot detect this. The same computation refutes the claim in the proof of Lemma 3.1.12 that the map φ*(M̂_{R/a,1}) → M̃_1 ⊗ Ŵ(R/a_R) 'depends only on T_0 and not on T'; so that proof inherits the defect as well as the statement. No erratum is registered against the DOI; the corrections are in KPZ26 (Forum Math. Pi 2026).

review.reason: I checked this against the page image and against KPZ26 (arXiv:2409.03689v3). §1.3.1 says: 'The construction of the isomorphism Ψ_RG in [KP18, 3.2.12] is not correct. Such an isomorphism only exists under the additional assumption that the Hodge embedding is very good … Lemma 3.2.14 and Propositions 3.2.17 and 3.3.13 of [KP18] require Ψ_RG'. See also Remark 5.1.17 (the 3.1.9 map depends on the normal decomposition; pointed out by M. Hoff) and Def. 5.2.5. The last preprint, arXiv:1512.01149v3, has the identical text. Transcription note: the printed word is calligraphic 𝒢 ('as 𝒢 is smooth'), not G. Within Lemma 3.2.14, (1) ⇒ (4) needs only some tensor-preserving Ψ_{R_G}, which exists by Corollary 3.2.11. The constant-mod-a_{R_E} property is used only for the versality of 𝒢_{R_E}, which (3) ⇒ (2) and Proposition 3.2.17 use. Independent check: I accept the revision. (a) Transcription: the image of printed p. 173 reads 'Note that this is possible as 𝒢 is smooth', with calligraphic 𝒢, so the fix is right. (b) Locator: printed p. 181 (3.3.11) makes the choice again: 'Then the assumptions in 3.2.12(2) are satisfied, and we may fix an isomorphism Ψ : M̃_1 ≅ M lifting Ψ_0, such that Ψ is constant modulo a_{R_E}, and such that its base change Ψ_{R_G} to Ŵ(R_G) respects the s_{α,0}.' This is the instance that Proposition 3.3.13 and §4.2 (Proposition 4.2.2: 'satisfying the conditions in 3.2.12') actually use, so it belongs in the locator. (c) The refinement on Lemma 3.2.14 is accurate. (1) ⇒ (4) uses only that the s_{α,0} are Frobenius invariant in M_{R_G}^⊗, i.e. that Ψ_{R_G} preserves the tensors; Corollary 3.2.11 gives such a Ψ_{R_G}. Constancy mod a_{R_E} enters only through Lemma 3.1.12 (versality of 𝒢_{R_E}). That is used in (3) ⇒ (2) ('injective by the versality of 𝒢_{R_E}', p. 175) and in Proposition 3.2.17 ('By versality, we may lift', p. 176). The display M_{R_G}, and hence the statement of 3.2.14 itself, still refers to the chosen Ψ. KPZ26 §1.3.1 confirms: 'The construction of the isomorphism Ψ_RG in [KP18, 3.2.12] is not correct … Lemma 3.2.14 and Propositions 3.2.17 and 3.3.13 of [KP18] require Ψ_RG'. arXiv v3 has the same text in 3.2.12 and 3.3.11. Classification: 'error' is justified. The printed justification ('as 𝒢 is smooth') fails, and it rests on the non-canonical map of Lemma 3.1.9 (E1). The authors call it 'not correct' and 'the error'. One nuance for the record: KPZ26 §1.2.1 (p. 6) conjectures that every good integral Hodge embedding is very good. So the dependent statements are unproved in the stated generality, not known to be false.

The proof of Proposition 4.2.2 (p. 185) equips D ⊗_W R with a display 'satisfying the conditions in 3.2.12' and then invokes 3.3.13 (printed 'Lemma 3.3.13'). KPZ26 §1.3.1 says both need Ψ_{R_G}, which exists only for very good embeddings. The KPZ26 proof of Thm. 7.1.3 says explicitly that 'the argument in [KP18, Prop. 4.2.2, Thm. 4.2.7]' works under assumption (C). Corollary 4.2.4 is deduced only from 4.2.2 (p. 186). Then Y = 𝒮^-_K ×_{𝒮_{K_1}(GSp)} 𝒮_{K'_1}(GSp) is finite étale over 𝒮^-_K, and Sh_{K'} is open and closed in Y_E. So 𝒮^-_{K'} is a union of irreducible components of the flat scheme Y. Normalization commutes with étale base change, so 𝒮_{K'} is a union of connected components of Y ×_{𝒮^-_K} 𝒮_K, which is finite étale over 𝒮_K. review.reason: E4's claim that the printed assertion is 'simply false' is too strong. An action morphism a: 𝒢 × M → M is itself a trivial 𝒢-torsor for h·(g,m) = (gh^{-1}, hm): the shear (g,m) ↦ (g, gm) turns a into pr_2. Concretely, 𝒢_W (identified with 𝒢 ⊗ W in 3.3.9 and in the proof of 4.2.4) acts freely and transitively on the fibres of q^loc via (f,ℱ) ↦ (f∘g^{-1}, gℱ), and m ↦ (f_0, f_0^{-1}m) is a section. What fails is that q^loc is not a torsor for the 𝒢-action on f through V^∨, for which π^loc is a torsor and (4.2.8) is equivariant; so 'π^loc and q^loc are 𝒢-torsors' cannot hold for one and the same action. The proof uses only that q^loc is smooth of relative dimension dim G ('Since q^loc has the required properties, so does q'), and that holds in either reading. KPZ26 §7.3.1(1) is the authors' own erratum and gives the right replacement. Independent check: Quotation checked on p. 187 (zoomed). I re-derived the revision independently. Write q^loc(f,ℱ) = f(ℱ) (see E57). 𝒢_W = Aut(D_x̄, s_{α,0,x̄}) ≅ 𝒢 ⊗ W (3.3.9) acts on M̃^loc_G by h·(f,ℱ) = (f∘h^{-1}, hℱ). This action preserves M^loc_G, because M^loc_G is the flat closure of a G_{K_0}-orbit. It is free, and it is transitive on the fibres of q^loc: if f(ℱ) = f'(ℱ'), then h = f'^{-1}f works. It has the section m ↦ (f_0, f_0^{-1}m), where f_0 is a W-point of the trivial torsor 𝒫. Here f_0^{-1}m ∈ M^loc_G because f_0 carries the orbit closure of y(x) (type μ_h^{-1}) onto M^loc_{G,X} ⊗ O_{E^ur}. So the printed 'q^loc is a 𝒢-torsor' is true for this action, and E4's 'simply false' is too strong. It is false for the V^∨-side action g·(f,ℱ) = (g∘f, ℱ), for which π^loc is a torsor and q^loc is equivariant. No single free 𝒢-action makes both maps torsors unless μ is central, since orbits would lie in the fibres of (π^loc, q^loc), which have dimension dim 𝒢 − dim(orbit of ℱ). The authors' erratum (KPZ26 §7.3.1(1)) is itself loose: the action morphism 𝒢 × M → M is a trivial torsor for h·(g,m) = (gh^{-1}, hm). The proof uses only 'q^loc is smooth of relative dimension dim G', and that holds either way. So the defect is an unspecified or conflated group action, with nothing lost.

The failing step is the sentence 'Since K°_p ∩ Ã(G_{Z_(p)})° is contained in the kernel …': an element t of K°_p ∩ Ã° fixes the coset a·j·K°_{2,p} only if j^{-1}(a^{-1}ta)j ∈ K°_{2,p}, which holds for j = 1 (or j normalizing K°_{2,p}) but not in general; the stabilizer of the j-th coset is jK°_pj^{-1} ∩ Ã°. The printed statement then drops j altogether and writes a |J|-th power. arXiv:1512.01149v2 carries the same text. The torsor (4.6.20) is formed by the identical recipe and inherits the error. Independent check: Quotations checked on the images of pp. 202, 203 and 205 (Lemma 4.6.13, the proof's display (4.6.14) and the sentence 'Since K°_p ∩ Ã(G_{Z_(p)})° is contained in the kernel…', (4.6.16), (4.6.20)). To pass to Sh_{K°_p}(G,X)^+ the text needs N = K°_p ∩ Ã° to act trivially on this set. An element t ∈ N maps into the normal subgroup K°_{2,p} of Ã(G_{2,Z_(p)}), so t·a·j·K°_{2,p} = a·j·(j^{-1}(a^{-1}ta)j)·K°_{2,p}. review.reason: Image of p. 135 confirms the wording. H here is an arbitrary split connected reductive group (§1.1.2, §1.2.12), and Aut(H)(K̃) = H^ad(K̃) ⋊ Aut(based root datum). The automorphism group of the based root datum is not in general the automorphism group of the Dynkin diagram. For a torus, e.g. Res_{K'/K}G_m, the diagram is empty but Ξ = Aut(X^•) ≠ 1. For GL_2, which is relevant to U(2) and GU(1,1), the A_1 diagram has no automorphisms, yet transpose-inverse is outer. For SO_8, triality does not preserve the character lattice. Read literally, every torus would be split. The parenthetical identification with pinning-preserving automorphisms is correct, and it is what the paper uses (§1.2.15 ff.; §2.1.4 sets Ξ_H = Aut(R^+)).

sourceIssues.reason: If K_1/K has a nontrivial unramified part (f_1 > 1, possible when k is finite), then Res_{K_1/K}(GL(V)_D) ⊗_K K^ur is a product of f_1 copies of Res_{K_1^ur/K^ur}(GL(V)_D ⊗ K_1^ur), and V ⊗_{K_1} K_1^ur has K^ur-dimension dim_K V / f_1. A single chain of lattices in V ⊗_{K_1} K_1^ur is then not a lattice chain in V ⊗_K K^ur, and the single-factor map is neither G(K^ur)- nor Frobenius-equivariant. Example: G = Res_{K'/K}GL_n with K'/K unramified quadratic and V = K'^n (dim_K V = 2n). Here D = K_1 = K', K_1^ur = K^ur, GL(V)_D ⊗ K^ur = GL_n, and G(K^ur) = GL_n(K^ur)². Case for the defence: for k algebraically closed (K^ur = K), or K_1/K totally ramified, the text is correct as written. The intended construction is standard, the existence of the equivariant ι in (1.2.26) and all later uses (§1.3.1, Prop. 1.3.3, §2.3) stand, and §1.3 itself uses the correct product. For finite k, O_K[[u]] is complete, hence henselian, but its residue field k_K (a finite extension of k) is not separably closed, so the ring is not strictly henselian. review.reason: Image of p. 145 confirms the quote. In §1.4, k may be finite: §1.4.1 continues the notation of §1.1.1, Lemma 1.4.5 invokes 'our assumptions on k', and Step 4 of Prop. 1.4.3 treats 'any k'. Lemma 1.4.6 carries no restriction on k. For finite k, 𝒦 = Frac(W(k)[[u]]) does not have cohomological dimension 2. The prime (p) of the excellent ring W[[u]] gives a decomposition group ≅ Gal(ℰ), a closed subgroup of Gal(𝒦), where ℰ = K_0{{u}} is complete discretely valued with residue field k((u)). For ℓ ≠ p, cd_ℓ(ℰ) = 1 + cd_ℓ(k((u))) = 1 + 1 + cd_ℓ(k) = 3 (Serre, Galois Cohomology II.4.3). So cd_ℓ(𝒦) ≥ 3, and in fact = 3 by Hochschild–Serre over the strict henselisation. The cd-2 results cited (Gabber; Kato/Kuzumaki [47]) need a separably closed residue field. Hence Serre's Conjecture II (Gille [28]) cannot be applied, and the proof of H^1(𝒦,G) = 1, and with it the lemma, fails for finite k. I do not know whether the statement is true for finite k. The lemma is used only in Step 2, under k algebraically closed; finite k is handled by base change to O_L in Step 4. So Prop. 1.4.3 is unaffected, but Lemma 1.4.6 as stated is unproved in part of its range. Not in the KPZ26 corrections.

sourceIssues.reason: Step 3 applies Bruhat–Tits theory to G over ℰ = K_0{{u}}, whose residue field k((u)) is imperfect. It tacitly identifies the O_ℰ-points of the W-group schemes 𝒢, 𝒢_i, 𝒯° with the corresponding Bruhat–Tits subgroups of G(ℰ), without comment. In the defence, both points are routine for the quasi-split G_{K_0}. I found no statement of them in KP18 and no correction in KPZ26 (§1.3.1, §7.3). The later purity results [An22], [PR24] cited by KPZ26 p. 76 cover this case independently.

review.reason: Images of pp. 147–148 confirm the quotes. Step 3 works with O_ℰ-points of the W-group schemes 𝒢, 𝒢_i, 𝒯° and applies Bruhat–Tits results ([11] 4.4.14, 5.2.4, 5.2.11) to G(ℰ), where ℰ = K_0{{u}} has imperfect residue field k((u)). Two identifications are used without comment. (a) 𝒢(O_ℰ) = q_i^{-1}(B_i(k((u)))) needs 𝒢 to be the dilatation of 𝒢_i along the preimage of B_i in the special fibre. This follows from [11, (1.7.6)] with k algebraically closed, because both are smooth W-models with the same W-points; for p-torsion-free O_ℰ the dilatation's points are exactly that preimage. (b) 'G(ℰ)^1 coincides with the subgroup generated by all parahoric subgroups of G(ℰ) considered in [11, 5.2.11]' needs the 𝒢_i ⊗_W O_ℰ and 𝒯° ⊗_W O_ℰ to be the Bruhat–Tits parahoric and connected Néron group schemes of G_ℰ, with the alcove of x in B(G,K_0) matching one in B(G,ℰ). This holds because ℰ/K_0 has ramification index 1 and G_{K_0} is quasi-split (k algebraically closed) and split by the totally ramified K_0(p^{1/e}), which stays a degree-e field over ℰ; so the relative root system and the affine root valuations do not change. Both are routine, but the paper does not state them. KPZ26 does not correct this; later purity results ([An22], [PR24], cited by KPZ26) cover the statement independently.

Only type (a) is argued, and there only the input is supplied: Satake's factorization, Landvogt's toral map ι'_1 into B(U(V'_1/D,h_1)), and its agreement with t+ι_1 of (1.2.23). review.reason: The claim is real, but it is a false step, not merely an omission, so the kind is error. Quotations checked on printed pp. 158–159. By §1.2.15 (p. 136), V_j⊗Q̃_p ≅ ⊕_i V(λ_{ji})^{⊕m_j}⊗Q̃_p, where m_j is the degree of the centralizer division algebra D_j of ρ_j. The printed V'_j = (V(λ_{j1})⊗Q̃_p)^{I_{j1}} has L_j-dimension dim V(λ_{j1}), and the τ's are in bijection with the I-orbits in the Γ-orbit of λ_{j1}. So dim_L V_L = Σ_j dim_{Q_p}V_j / m_j. Hence 'ρ_L can be identified with G_L → ∏_j∏_τ GL(V'_{j,L}) ⊂ GL(V_L)' and 'y = ι(x) ∈ B(GL(V),Q_p) ⊂ B(GL(V_L),L)' are false as soon as some m_j > 1, because the Res_{D/K_1} step of (1.2.17) has been dropped. The case occurs in practice. Check of the first reading's example: G = D^× (D quaternion division over Q_p) acting on V = D by left multiplication, with ψ(x,y) = Trd(x a ȳ), a pure. Then ψ(gx,gy) = Nrd(g)ψ(x,y), ψ is alternating and perfect, G_{Q̄_p} = GL_2 with V = std^{⊕2}, μ = (1,0) gives ρ∘μ ~ diag(a^{(2)},1^{(2)}), scalars lie in G, and G^der is simply connected. So this is a local Hodge embedding (the Shimura-curve situation at a ramified p) with m = 2, dim V = 4 and dim V_L = 2. The same example shows that the first reading's correction is right: O_D⊗W is an Iwahori order in M_2(W), and the O_D-chain {Π^n O_D} gives two copies of the same edge-midpoint chain of GL_2, shifted by one step relative to each other. So y over L is a sum of translates y'+t_i, not a single copy. Omitting the τ-twist in '∏_τ ρ'_{j,L}' is only notational, since the τ's are declared to index the conjugate weights. Prop. 2.3.7 itself is not in doubt, and the repair is routine. KPZ26 does not mention this.

So K_p = K_p° only says π_0(𝒢_{F_p}) has no nontrivial F_p-point. I re-derived the counterexample. Let T = R^1_{L/Q_p}G_m with L = Q_p(p^{1/3}) and p ≡ 2 mod 3, p ≠ 2. T is tame and anisotropic. The Galois closure has group S_3, with inertia A_3 and Frobenius a transposition, and X_*(T) is the augmentation lattice ≅ Z[ζ_3]. Then X_*(T)_I = Z/3 and the transposition acts on it by −1. So π_0(𝒯_{F̄_p}) = Z/3 but its F_p-points are trivial: T(Q_p) = 𝒯°(Z_p) although 𝒯 ≠ 𝒯°. Over F_{p^2}, π_0 and H^1(F_{p^2}, π_0) = Z/3 are nontrivial. So in 4.2.13 (arbitrary F_q ⊃ k_E), 'the smooth connected group scheme 𝒢_{F_q}' does not follow from the hypothesis, and the fibre π^{-1}(z) may be a nontrivial torsor. The geometric strata of 4.2.12 are L^+𝒢°-orbits. Elements of 𝒢(Z̆_p) ∖ 𝒢°(Z̆_p) act on them through conjugation by Ω-elements, which can permute Adm(μ)^K, so descent along π needs 𝒢_k-stable strata. review.reason: Checked on pp. 192–193. For A = Z_(p) and a base with fibres of characteristic p, the identity component of the kernel of a homomorphism of abelian schemes need not be flat or an abelian scheme. the first reading's example is right: on the sum-zero part K ≅ E^{p−1} of E^p, the fixed points of the cyclic permutation are the diagonal E[p], whose identity component is trivial in characteristic 0 and infinitesimal (E[p]°) in characteristic p. This is exactly what happens when the Galois module A' ⊗ Z_(p) contains the augmentation lattice, as for a wildly ramified cyclic A' (Noether), and then ker(f)° ⊇ 𝒜[p]°-type pieces. A second loose step has the same cause: 'the cokernel of B ⊂ 𝒜^𝒫 is a torsion sheaf, so B ⊗_A A' → 𝒜 ⊗_A A' is an isomorphism' needs that torsion to be killed by an integer invertible in A. Both steps are fine when |Gal(Fr A'/Q)| ∈ A^×, or when A' ⊗ Z_(p) is étale over Z_(p), since then A' is locally free over A[Gal] (normal basis) and taking invariants is exact. In the paper's favour: in 4.5 the lemma is applied to the universal object over the normal flat 𝒮_K(G,X). There B can be taken as the closure of the abelian subvariety of the generic fibre, which extends over a normal base, and nothing suggests the lemma's conclusion fails. Not corrected in KPZ26.

- F is a non-Galois totally real cubic field (Galois closure F̃ with group S_3), and p = 𝔭_1𝔭_2 with f(𝔭_2) = 2.

review.reason: Checked at 300 dpi on p. 213: 'φ_r(w) = Tr^ss(Frob_y, RΨ^{M^loc}_w̄)'. φ_r is a function on M^loc(F_q), and there is no y. By (4.7.7) the intended term is Frob_w. the first reading's second point is also right. The paper itself says w is 'well-defined up to the action of 𝒢^{ad°}(F_q)', since π in (4.7.5) is a 𝒢^{ad°}-torsor. Yet q is written with target 𝒢°(F_q)\M^loc(F_q). 𝒢° acts through 𝒢°(F_q) → 𝒢^{ad°}(F_q), which is not surjective in general: its cokernel is governed by H^1(F_q) of the kernel. So the natural target is 𝒢^{ad°}(F_q)\M^loc(F_q). φ_r is 𝒢^{ad°}(F_q)-invariant (q is 𝒢^{ad°}-equivariant, and (4.7.7) holds for every choice of w), so ψ_r = φ_r∘q is well defined. φ_r is then in particular 𝒢°(F_q)-invariant, so §§4.7.8–4.7.10 are unaffected.
